title.zh: 卷四十六 吳書一 孫破虜討逆傳
title.en: Volume 46: Book of Wu 1 - Biographies of Sun Who Destroys Barbarians, and Sun Who Attacks Rebels
title.raw: 卷四十六 吳書一 孫破虜討逆傳 Volume 46: Book of Wu 1 - Biographies of Sun Who Destroys Barbarians, and Sun Who Attacks Rebels

sentences.zh: 孫堅 孫策

translations.literal: Sun Jian; Sun Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian and Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 孫堅字文臺，吳郡富春人，蓋孫武之後也。

translations.literal: Sun Jian, courtesy name Wentai, was a man of Fuchun in Wu Commandery; he was in the line of descent from Sun Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian, whose courtesy name was Wentai, came from Fuchun in Wu Commandery and claimed descent from Sun Wu.

sentences.zh: 〈吳書曰：堅世仕吳，家於富春，葬於城東。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: For generations the Suns had served in Wu, made their home in Fuchun, and were buried east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Wu, the Sun family had long served in Wu, settled at Fuchun, and buried their dead east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 塚上數有光怪，雲氣五色，上屬於天，曼延數里。

translations.literal: On the mound there were often strange lights; five-colored vapors linked up to Heaven and stretched for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Strange lights often played above the tomb, and bands of five-colored mist rose to meet the sky, trailing for miles along the ground.

sentences.zh: 眾皆往觀視。

translations.literal: The crowd all went to look.
translations.idiomatic: People flocked from all around to see it.

sentences.zh: 父老相謂曰：「是非凡氣，孫氏其興矣！

translations.literal: The village elders said to one another, “This is no ordinary aura—the house of Sun is about to rise!”
translations.idiomatic: The elders murmured among themselves, “That is no common omen; the Sun clan is destined to flourish.”

sentences.zh: 」及母懷妊堅，夢腸出繞吳昌門，寤而懼之，以告鄰母。

translations.literal: When his mother was pregnant with Jian, she dreamed that her intestines came out and wound around the Wu Chang Gate; waking, she was frightened and told a neighbor woman.
translations.idiomatic: While carrying Sun Jian, his mother dreamed her entrails spilled forth and coiled around Wu’s Chang Gate; she woke in terror and confided in a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 鄰母曰：「安知非吉徵也。

translations.literal: The neighbor woman said, “How do you know it is not an auspicious sign?”
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor replied, “Who can say it is not a blessing in disguise?”

sentences.zh: 」堅生，容貌不凡，性闊達，好奇節。〉

translations.literal: When Jian was born, his appearance was extraordinary; his nature was broad-minded and he admired striking conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian was born with striking features, an open disposition, and a taste for bold, principled deeds.〉

sentences.zh: 少為縣吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk in the county.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 年十七，與父共載船至錢唐，會海賊胡玉等從匏裡上掠取賈人財物，方於岸上分之，行旅皆住，船不敢進。

translations.literal: At seventeen, he and his father were together in a boat going to Qiantang, when pirates Hu Yu and others came up from inside a gourd to plunder merchants’ goods; they were on the shore dividing the spoil, travelers all halted, and boats dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he shared a boat with his father bound for Qiantang when the bandit Hu Yu and his gang emerged from a reed covert to rob merchants; the robbers were ashore splitting the loot, and every craft hung back, afraid to pass.

sentences.zh: 堅謂父曰：「此賊可擊，請討之。

translations.literal: Jian said to his father, “These bandits can be attacked; I beg to go punish them.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian told his father, “We can take those thieves—let me deal with them.”

sentences.zh: 」父曰：「非爾所圖也。

translations.literal: His father said, “This is not for you to plan.”
translations.idiomatic: His father answered, “That is no business of yours.”

sentences.zh: 」堅行操刀上岸，以手東西指麾，若分部人兵以羅遮賊狀。

translations.literal: Jian took a knife, went ashore, and with his hands gestured east and west as if deploying troops in formation to encircle the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian seized a blade, waded ashore, and waved his arms this way and that as though he were deploying soldiers to trap the raiders.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，以為官兵捕之，即委財物散走。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing him, thought government troops were coming to seize them; at once they abandoned the goods and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates mistook him for an official force and dropped their plunder, fleeing in panic.

sentences.zh: 堅追，斬得一級以還。

translations.literal: Jian pursued them, cut off one head, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He gave chase, took one head, and came back.

sentences.zh: 父大驚。

translations.literal: His father was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: His father stared in amazement.

sentences.zh: 由是顯聞，府召署假尉。

translations.literal: Thereby he became famous; the prefect summoned him and appointed him acting commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the deed spread, and the prefect called him in and named him acting commandant.

sentences.zh: 會稽妖賊許昌起於句章，自稱陽明皇帝，

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Xu Chang of Kuaiji rose at Gouzhang, calling himself Emperor of Yangming,
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji the sectarian rebel Xu Chang broke out at Gouzhang and proclaimed himself the Yangming Emperor,

sentences.zh: 〈灵帝纪曰：昌以其父为越王也。〉

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Ling states: Chang made his father King of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling’s annals note that Xu Chang had his father styled King of Yue.〉

sentences.zh: 與其子韶扇動諸縣，眾以萬數。

translations.literal: Together with his son Shao he stirred up the counties, and their followers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He and his son Shao incited the counties until their host ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 堅以郡司馬募召精勇，得千餘人，與州郡合討破之。

translations.literal: Jian, as county marshal, recruited picked brave men, obtained more than a thousand, and with the province and commanderies jointly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian, serving as county marshal, raised over a thousand picked fighters and, joining the provincial and local forces, crushed the rising.

sentences.zh: 是歲，熹平元年也。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first year of the Xiping era (172).

sentences.zh: 刺史臧旻列上功狀，詔書除堅鹽瀆丞，數歲徙盱眙丞，又徙下邳丞。

translations.literal: The Inspector Zang Min listed his merits in a memorial; an edict appointed Jian assistant magistrate of Yandu; after several years he was transferred to magistrate of Xuyi, then again to magistrate of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zang Min reported his service to the throne; an edict named him assistant magistrate of Yandu, and after a few years he was moved to Xuyi, then to Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：坚历佐三县，所在有称，吏民亲附。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Jian successively assisted three counties; wherever he went he was praised, and clerks and commoners grew attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says Sun Jian served three counties in turn, won praise at each posting, and drew officials and people to his side.

sentences.zh: 乡里知旧，好事少年，往来者常数百人，坚接抚待养，有若子弟焉。〉

translations.literal: Townsmen and old friends, and adventurous youths who came and went, were often several hundred in number; Jian received and supported them as if they were his own sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of local friends and restless young men drifted in and out of his circle, and he fed and housed them like family.〉

sentences.zh: 邊章、韓遂作亂涼州，中郎將董卓拒討無功。

translations.literal: Bian Zhang and Han Sui made rebellion in Liangzhou; Colonel Dong Zhuo resisted and attacked them without success.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Zhang and Han Sui revolted in Liangzhou, Colonel Dong Zhuo led the campaign against them and accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 中平三年，遣司空張溫行車騎將軍，西討章等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongping, the court sent Minister of Works Zhang Wen to act as General of Chariots and Cavalry and march west to punish Zhang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongping 3 (186) the court dispatched Minister of Works Zhang Wen, acting as General of Chariots and Cavalry, on a western expedition against Bian Zhang’s coalition.

sentences.zh: 溫表請堅與參軍事，屯長安。

translations.literal: Wen memorialized asking that Jian join the staff on military affairs and encamp at Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen petitioned to have Sun Jian serve on his staff and garrison Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 溫以詔書召卓，卓良久乃詣溫。

translations.literal: Wen used an edict to summon Zhuo; Zhuo after a long time only then came to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen summoned Dong Zhuo by edict, and Dong Zhuo kept him waiting a long while before he appeared.

sentences.zh: 溫責讓卓，卓應對不順。

translations.literal: Wen rebuked Zhuo; Zhuo’s replies were insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen dressed him down; Dong Zhuo answered with open defiance.

sentences.zh: 堅時在坐，前耳語謂溫曰：「卓不怖罪而鴟張大語，宜以召不時至，陳軍法斬之。

translations.literal: Jian at the time was seated there; he leaned forward and whispered to Wen, “Zhuo does not fear guilt but crows arrogantly with big words; it is fitting, on the ground that he was slow to answer the summons, to execute him according to military law.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian, who was present, murmured to Zhang Wen, “Dong Zhuo shows no fear of punishment—only swagger. Execute him for tardiness to the summons; military law demands it.”

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「卓素著威名於隴蜀之間，今日殺之，西行無依。

translations.literal: Wen said, “Zhuo has long enjoyed a fearsome name between Long and Shu; if we kill him today, on the march west we will have no support.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen replied, “Dong Zhuo’s dread reputation runs through Long and Ba; kill him now and the western column loses its backbone.”

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「明公親率王兵，威震天下，何賴於卓？

translations.literal: Jian said, “Your Lordship personally leads the king’s troops and awe shakes the world—why depend on Zhuo?”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian answered, “You command the imperial host in person and your name shakes the realm—what need have you of Dong Zhuo?”

sentences.zh: 觀卓所言，不假明公，輕上無禮，一罪也。

translations.literal: Look at Zhuo’s words: he does not defer to Your Lordship; he is disrespectful to his superiors and lacks propriety—that is the first crime.
translations.idiomatic: Listen to his tone: he bows to no one above him; that is insolence toward authority—his first offense.

sentences.zh: 章、遂跋扈經年，當以時進討，而卓雲未可，沮軍疑眾，二罪也。

translations.literal: Zhang and Sui have run rampant for years; the time has come to advance and punish them, yet Zhuo says it cannot be done—he dampens the army’s spirit and sows doubt in the ranks; that is the second crime.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Zhang and Han Sui have swaggered for years and ought to be struck now, yet Dong Zhuo says the moment is wrong—he saps morale and breeds mistrust; that is his second count.

sentences.zh: 卓受任無功，應召稽留，而軒昂自高，三罪也。

translations.literal: Zhuo received his commission without merit; he was summoned and tarried, yet he holds his head high—that is the third crime.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a command and achieved nothing, dallied when summoned, yet struts as though he were indispensable; that is his third crime.

sentences.zh: 古之名將，仗鉞臨眾，未有不斷斬以示威者也。

translations.literal: Among the famous generals of old, when they grasped the battle-axe and faced the host, there was never one who did not cut off a head to display awe.
translations.idiomatic: The great captains of old, axe in hand before their troops, always made an example with the executioner’s blade.

sentences.zh: 是以穰苴斬莊賈，魏絳戮楊干。

translations.literal: Therefore Rangju executed Zhuang Jia, and Wei Jiang put Yang Gan to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Tian Rangju beheaded Zhuang Jia, and Wei Jiang executed Yang Gan.

sentences.zh: 今明公垂意於卓，不即加誅，虧損威刑。

translations.literal: Now Your Lordship favors Zhuo and does not at once add execution; you injure awe and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If you indulge Dong Zhuo and spare him, you wound the majesty of the law.

sentences.zh: 於是在矣。

translations.literal: The moment is here.
translations.idiomatic: The case is before you now.

sentences.zh: 」溫不忍發舉，乃曰：「君且還，卓將疑人。

translations.literal: Wen could not bear to carry it out and said, “For the moment withdraw; Zhuo will begin to suspect people.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen shrank from the deed and told him, “Go back for now—Dong Zhuo will grow suspicious if we press further.”

sentences.zh: 」堅因起出。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon rose and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian rose and left.

sentences.zh: 章、遂聞大兵向至，黨眾離散，皆乞降。

translations.literal: When Zhang and Sui heard that a great army was coming, their factions scattered and all begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a great host was closing in, Bian Zhang and Han Sui’s followers melted away and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 軍還，議者以軍未臨敵，不斷功賞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, those who deliberated held that, because the army had not yet confronted the enemy, rewards for merit should not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal, the councilors argued that no battle had been joined, so merit pay should not yet be fixed.

sentences.zh: 然聞堅數卓三罪，勸溫斬之，無不歎息。

translations.literal: Yet when they heard that Jian enumerated Zhuo’s three crimes and urged Wen to behead him, there was none who did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everyone who heard how Sun Jian listed Dong Zhuo’s three offenses and urged Zhang Wen to strike drew a long breath in admiration.

sentences.zh: 拜堅議郎。

translations.literal: Jian was appointed Consultant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian was named Consultant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時長沙賊區星自稱將軍，眾萬餘人攻圍城邑，乃以堅為長沙太守。

translations.literal: At that time the Changsha bandit Qu Xing styled himself a general; with a host of more than ten thousand he attacked and besieged towns, so Jian was made Grand Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When the Changsha rebel Qu Xing, calling himself a general, led over ten thousand men against the cities, the court named Sun Jian Grand Administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 到郡親率將士，施設方略，旬月之間，克破星等。

translations.literal: Arriving in the commandery he personally led generals and soldiers, laid plans and stratagems, and within a month or so broke and destroyed Xing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He reached his jurisdiction, took the field in person, laid his plans, and within a month had smashed Qu Xing’s force.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书曰：坚到郡，郡中震服，任用良吏。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: When Jian reached the commandery, the whole commandery trembled into submission; he employed able officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records that his arrival awed the commandery into order and that he appointed capable men.〉

sentences.zh: 敕吏曰：「谨遇良善，治官曹文书，必循治，以盗贼付太守。」〉

translations.literal: He instructed the clerks, saying, “Treat the good with care; for office documents follow proper procedure; leave banditry to the Grand Administrator.”
translations.idiomatic: He told his clerks, “Cherish the law-abiding, keep the paperwork in good order, and hand robbers over to me.”〉

sentences.zh: 周朝、郭石亦帥徒眾起於零、桂，與星相應。

translations.literal: Zhou Chao and Guo Shi also led their followers and rose in Ling and Gui, responding to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chao and Guo Shi likewise raised bands in Lingling and Guiyang in concert with Qu Xing.

sentences.zh: 遂越境尋討，三郡肅然。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed boundaries to seek and punish them, and the three commanderies were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed his borders to hunt them down until three commanderies lay calm.

sentences.zh: 漢朝錄前後功，封堅為烏程侯。

translations.literal: The Han court recorded his successive merits and enfeoffed Jian as Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Han reckoned his earlier and later service and invested him as Marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：是时庐江太守陆康从子作宜春长，为贼所攻，遣使求救於坚。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: At that time Lu Kang, Grand Administrator of Lujiang, had a nephew serving as magistrate of Yichun; he was attacked by bandits and sent a messenger begging aid from Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu says Lu Kang of Lujiang had a nephew who was magistrate of Yichun; when bandits besieged him he appealed to Sun Jian.

sentences.zh: 坚整严救之。

translations.literal: Jian put his troops in good order and went to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian drew up his host and marched to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 主簿进谏，坚答曰：「太守无文德，以征伐为功，越界攻讨，以全异国。

translations.literal: The chief clerk remonstrated; Jian answered, saying, “A Grand Administrator who lacks civil virtue and wins his name by campaigning may cross boundaries to attack and thereby preserve another state.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk objected, but Sun Jian replied, “An administrator without literary polish earns his reputation in the field; I may cross a border to save a neighbor’s people.

sentences.zh: 以此获罪，何愧海内乎？

translations.literal: If I incur guilt for this, what shame would I have before the realm?”
translations.idiomatic: If that earns me blame, I will still have nothing to blush for under Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 」乃进兵往救，贼闻而走。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army to go save them; the bandits heard and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed his army forward; the raiders fled at the news.〉

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，卓擅朝政，橫恣京城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died, Zhuo monopolized court government and wantonly tyrannized the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling died, Dong Zhuo seized the government and ran riot in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 諸州郡並興義兵，欲以討卓。

translations.literal: The various provinces and commanderies together raised righteous troops intending to punish Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies everywhere raised loyal armies to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：坚闻之，拊膺叹曰：「张公昔从吾言，朝廷今无此难也。」〉

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: When Jian heard it, he beat his breast and sighed, saying, “If Lord Zhang had once listened to me, the court would not face this calamity today.”
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says Sun Jian smote his chest and cried, “Had Zhang Wen heeded me then, the capital would never be in this plight.”〉

sentences.zh: 堅亦舉兵。

translations.literal: Jian also raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian raised a force of his own.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王睿素遇堅無禮，堅過殺之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou, Wang Rui, had always treated Jian rudely; when Jian passed through he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, the Inspector of Jingzhou, had long slighted him, so Sun Jian cut him down as he passed through his territory.

sentences.zh: 〈案《王氏谱》，叡字通耀，晋太保祥伯父也。

translations.literal: According to the Wang lineage table, Rui’s courtesy name was Tongyao; he was the uncle by marriage of Grand Protector Wang Xiang of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang genealogy gives Rui the courtesy name Tongyao and makes him the uncle of Jin’s Grand Protector Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：叡先与坚共击零、桂贼，以坚武官，言颇轻之。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: Rui had earlier joined Jian in attacking the bandits of Ling and Gui; because Jian was a military officer, his words were rather contemptuous.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu adds that Wang Rui had campaigned with Sun Jian against Ling and Gui and, thinking him a mere fighting man, spoke down to him.

sentences.zh: 及叡举兵欲讨卓，素与武陵太守曹寅不相能，杨言当先杀寅。

translations.literal: When Rui raised troops intending to punish Zhuo, he had long been unable to get along with the Grand Administrator of Wuling, Cao Yin, and openly declared he would kill Yin first.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Rui mobilized against Dong Zhuo, he was on bad terms with Cao Yin of Wuling and vowed publicly to execute Yin first.

sentences.zh: 寅惧，诈作案行使者光禄大夫温毅檄，移坚，说叡罪过，令收行刑讫，以状上。

translations.literal: Yin was afraid; he forged a document in the name of the imperial agent, Guanglu dafu Wen Yi, shifting blame onto Rui and ordering Jian to seize him, carry out execution, and report the facts upward.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin, in fear, forged orders in the name of the credential-bearing envoy Guanglu dafu Wen Yi, listing Wang Rui’s crimes and instructing Sun Jian to arrest him, put him to death, and memorialize the result.

sentences.zh: 坚即承檄勒兵袭叡。

translations.literal: Jian at once accepted the document, mobilized troops, and raided Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian accepted the commission at once, mustered his men, and fell upon Wang Rui.

sentences.zh: 叡闻兵至，登楼望之，遣问欲何为，坚前部答曰：「兵久战劳苦，所得赏，不足以为衣服，诣使君更乞资直耳。

translations.literal: When Rui heard the army had arrived, he ascended a tower to look; he sent someone down to ask what they intended, and the van of Jian’s force answered, “The soldiers have fought long and hard; what they received in reward is not enough for clothing—we come to ask Your Excellency for more funds.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui climbed a tower to watch; he sent a man to ask their purpose, and Sun Jian’s vanguard replied, “We have marched until we are worn threadbare; our bonuses will not clothe us—we only beg the inspector for more pay.”

sentences.zh: 」叡曰：「刺史岂有所吝？

translations.literal: Rui said, “Would an Inspector be stingy?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui called back, “Would I begrudge you anything?”

sentences.zh: 」便开库藏，使自入视之，知有所遗不。

translations.literal: He then opened the treasury and had them enter themselves to look whether anything remained.
translations.idiomatic: He threw open the granaries and treasury and told them to help themselves and see whether anything was left.

sentences.zh: 兵进及楼下，叡见坚，惊曰：「兵自求赏，孙府君何以在其中？

translations.literal: When the troops reached the foot of the tower, Rui saw Jian and startled said, “The soldiers seek their own reward—why is Prefect Sun among them?”
translations.idiomatic: As they pressed the tower, Wang Rui spotted Sun Jian and exclaimed, “The men want their bounty—why is Magistrate Sun here?”

sentences.zh: 」坚曰：「被使者檄诛君。

translations.literal: Jian said, “I received the agent’s document ordering your execution.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian answered, “I hold orders from the envoy to put you to death.”

sentences.zh: 」叡曰：「我何罪？

translations.literal: Rui said, “What crime have I?”
translations.idiomatic: “What is my offense?”

sentences.zh: 」坚曰：「坐无所知。

translations.literal: Jian said, “Sitting in ignorance.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian said, “The crime of knowing nothing.”

sentences.zh: 」叡穷迫，刮金饮之而死。〉

translations.literal: Rui, driven to extremity, scraped gold and drank it and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wang Rui scraped gold dust, swallowed it, and died.〉

sentences.zh: 比至南陽，眾數萬人。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Nanyang, his followers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Nanyang his column had swelled into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守張咨聞軍至，晏然自若。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator of Nanyang, Zhang Zi, heard the army had come and remained calmly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi, Grand Administrator of Nanyang, heard the army was coming yet sat unruffled.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄记》曰：咨字子议，颍川人，亦知名。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji states: Zi’s courtesy name was Ziyi; he was a man of Yingchuan and was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji gives Zhang Zi the courtesy name Ziyi, from Yingchuan, and notes his reputation.

sentences.zh: 《献帝春秋》曰：袁术表坚假中郎将。

translations.literal: The Chunqiu of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu memorialized asking that Jian be named acting General of the Household Who Smashes the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian Emperor Annals record that Yuan Shu petitioned to appoint Sun Jian acting General of the Household Who Smashes the Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 坚到南阳，移檄太守请军粮。

translations.literal: When Jian reached Nanyang, he sent a summons asking the Grand Administrator for army grain.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Nanyang, Sun Jian sent a requisition to the grand administrator for provisions.

sentences.zh: 咨以问纲纪，纲纪曰：「坚邻郡二千石，不应调发。

translations.literal: Zi asked his chief clerk; the chief clerk said, “Jian is a neighboring commandery’s two-thousand-dan official; he should not be requisitioned.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi consulted his chief clerk, who answered, “Sun Jian is another commandery’s two-thousand-dan officer—you owe him no levy.”

sentences.zh: 」咨遂不与。〉

translations.literal: Zi therefore did not give.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi refused.〉

sentences.zh: 堅以牛酒禮咨，咨明日亦答詣堅。

translations.literal: Jian used oxen and wine to treat Zi with courtesy; the next day Zi also returned the courtesy and visited Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian feasted him with oxen and wine; the next day Zhang Zi came to return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，長沙主簿入白堅：「前移南陽，而道路不治，軍資不具，請收主簿推問意故。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, the chief clerk of Changsha entered and reported to Jian, saying, “The earlier march through Nanyang had roads not repaired and military supplies not prepared; I beg to seize the chief clerk and press the reason.”
translations.idiomatic: Mid-feast the Changsha chief clerk stepped in to Sun Jian: “Our passage through Nanyang found the roads unmended and no supplies laid in—arrest your chief clerk and ask why.”

sentences.zh: 」咨大懼欲去，兵陳四周不得出。

translations.literal: Zi was greatly frightened and wished to leave; troops were drawn up on four sides and he could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi tried to rise, but rings of soldiers penned him in.

sentences.zh: 有頃，主簿復入白堅：「南陽太守稽停義兵，使賊不時討，請收出案軍法從事。

translations.literal: After a little, the chief clerk again entered and reported to Jian, saying, “The Grand Administrator of Nanyang has obstructed the righteous army and kept the bandits from being punished in time; I beg to seize him out and deal with him according to military law.”
translations.idiomatic: Moments later the chief clerk returned: “The Grand Administrator of Nanyang has blocked the loyal host and delayed the strike against the rebels—take him out and try him by military law.”

sentences.zh: 」便牽咨於軍門斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they dragged Zi to the army gate and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled Zhang Zi to the camp gate and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 郡中震慄，無求不獲。

translations.literal: The whole commandery trembled in fear; there was no request that was not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery shook with dread, and from then on every demand was met.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：初坚至南阳，咨既不给军粮，又不肯见坚。

translations.literal: The Wu Li states: When Jian first reached Nanyang, Zi would neither supply army grain nor consent to see Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Li says that at first Zhang Zi neither issued grain nor would receive Sun Jian.

sentences.zh: 坚欲进兵，恐有后患，乃诈得急疾，举军震惶，迎呼巫医，祷祀山川。

translations.literal: Jian wished to advance the army but feared there would be later trouble; therefore he pretended to have fallen suddenly ill, and the whole army was shaken in alarm, calling in shamans and physicians and praying at mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to march on but fearing trouble in the rear, Sun Jian feigned a sudden illness; the camp erupted in panic, shamans and doctors were summoned, and sacrifices were offered to hill and stream gods.

sentences.zh: 遣所亲人说咨，言病困，欲以兵付咨。

translations.literal: He sent someone close to him to persuade Zi, saying he was gravely ill and wished to hand the troops over to Zi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a confidant to Zhang Zi, claiming he was dying and wished to entrust the army to him.

sentences.zh: 咨闻之，心利其兵，即将步骑五六百人诣营省坚。

translations.literal: When Zi heard it, his heart coveted the troops; he immediately led infantry and cavalry of five or six hundred men to the camp to visit Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zi, greedy for the command, rode straight to camp with five or six hundred horse and foot to inquire after Sun Jian.

sentences.zh: 坚卧与相见。

translations.literal: Jian lay down and met with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian received him from his couch.

sentences.zh: 无何，卒然而起，按剑骂咨，遂执斩之。

translations.literal: Before long, he suddenly rose, grasped his sword, reviled Zi, and thereupon seized and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In an instant he sprang up, sword in hand, cursed Zhang Zi, seized him, and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 此语与本传不同。〉

translations.literal: This language differs from the principal biography.
translations.idiomatic: This version disagrees with the main text.〉

sentences.zh: 前到魯陽，與袁術相見。

translations.literal: Advancing, he reached Luyang and met Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Luyang and joined Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術表堅行破虜將軍，領豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized asking that Jian act as General Who Smashes the Caitiffs and concurrently Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu petitioned the throne to appoint Sun Jian General Who Smashes the Caitiffs and acting Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂治兵於魯陽城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drilled troops at Luyang city.
translations.idiomatic: There he trained his army inside the walls of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 當進軍討卓，遣長史公仇稱將兵從事還州督促軍糧。

translations.literal: When about to advance the army to punish Zhuo, he sent Chief Clerk Gongqiu Cheng leading troops on assignment back to the province to hurry military grain.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to march against Dong Zhuo, he dispatched Chief Clerk Gongqiu Cheng with an escort to the province to press for the delivery of provisions.

sentences.zh: 施帳幔於城東門外，祖道送稱，官屬並會。

translations.literal: He spread curtains and hangings outside the east gate of the city, performed the road-leaving rite to send Cheng off, and officials and subordinates all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the east gate he pitched canopies for the farewell banquet for Cheng, and every officer in his staff turned out.

sentences.zh: 卓遣步騎數萬人逆堅，輕騎數十先到。

translations.literal: Zhuo dispatched infantry and cavalry numbering in the tens of thousands to oppose Jian; several tens of light cavalry arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent tens of thousands of foot and horse against him, and a few dozen light horsemen reached the scene first.

sentences.zh: 堅方行酒談笑，敕部曲整頓行陳，無得妄動。

translations.literal: Jian was just passing wine and talking and laughing; he ordered his units to put the battle lines in order and not to move rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian went on pouring wine and chatting calmly while ordering his men to dress the ranks and hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 後騎漸益，堅徐罷坐，導引入城。

translations.literal: The rear cavalry gradually increased; Jian slowly ended sitting, guided and led them into the city.
translations.idiomatic: As more enemy horsemen arrived, he rose without haste, saw his men through the gates, and withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 乃謂左右曰：「向堅所以不即起者，恐兵相蹈藉，諸君不得入耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to those at his side, “The reason I just now did not immediately rise was fearing the soldiers would trample one another and you gentlemen would not be able to enter.”
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers, “I stayed seated so our men would not panic and crush each other in the gateway—you needed a clear path in.”

sentences.zh: 」卓兵見堅士眾甚整，不敢攻城，乃引還。

translations.literal: Zhuo’s troops saw Jian’s soldiers were very orderly and did not dare attack the city; thereupon they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo’s host saw how steady Sun Jian’s ranks were and dared not storm the walls; they turned back.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄记》曰：初坚讨董卓，到梁县之阳人。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji states: When Jian first campaigned against Dong Zhuo, he reached Yangren in Liang County.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji records that Sun Jian’s first move against Dong Zhuo brought him to Yangren in Liang County.

sentences.zh: 卓亦遣兵步骑五千迎之，陈郡太守胡轸为大督护，吕布为骑督，其餘步骑将校都督者甚众。

translations.literal: Zhuo also dispatched troops, five thousand infantry and cavalry, to meet him; Grand Administrator of Chen Commandery Hu Zhen was chief overseer, Lü Bu was cavalry overseer, and the rest of infantry and cavalry commanders and overseers were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo likewise sent five thousand mixed troops to intercept him, with Hu Zhen of Chen as overall commander, Lü Bu as cavalry director, and a host of other colonels and captains under them.

sentences.zh: 轸字文才，性急，预宣言曰：「今此行也，要当斩一青绶，乃整齐耳。

translations.literal: Zhen’s courtesy name was Wencai; his nature was hasty, and he declared in advance, saying, “On this march we must behead one green-ribbon official, and only then will we be in good order.”
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen, courtesy Wencai, was a hothead who announced beforehand, “This time we cut down one man in the green sash—only then will the army know discipline.”

sentences.zh: 」诸将闻而恶之。

translations.literal: The various generals heard it and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The generals took the remark as a threat against themselves and loathed him.

sentences.zh: 军到广成，去阳人城数十里。

translations.literal: The army reached Guangcheng, several tens of li from Yangren city.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Guangcheng, still dozens of li short of Yangren.

sentences.zh: 日暮，士马疲极，当止宿，又本受卓节度宿广成，秣马饮食，以夜进兵，投晓攻城。

translations.literal: As the sun set, soldiers and horses were extremely weary; they ought to halt and encamp, and moreover originally received Zhuo’s orders to encamp at Guangcheng, feed the horses and eat, and by night advance troops, at dawn attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Night was falling, men and mounts were spent, and Dong Zhuo’s orders had been to bivouac at Guangcheng, rest and feed the horses, then march by night and storm the walls at dawn.

sentences.zh: 诸将恶惮轸，欲贼败其事，布等宣言「阳人城中贼已走，当追寻之；

translations.literal: The various generals feared and resented Zhen, wished to spoil and defeat the affair, and Bu and others declared, “The bandits in Yangren city have already fled; we ought to pursue and seek them;
translations.idiomatic: The commanders, nursing a grudge against Hu Zhen, resolved to wreck his plan; Lü Bu and his fellows spread word that “the rebels have already slipped out of Yangren—we must chase them now;

sentences.zh: 不然失之矣」，便夜进军。

translations.literal: if not, we will lose them,” and thereupon by night advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: or we lose them for good,” and so they pushed the column forward in the dark.

sentences.zh: 城中守备甚设，不可掩袭。

translations.literal: Defenses inside the city were very complete; they could not be taken by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yangren’s defenses were fully manned; a sneak attack was impossible.

sentences.zh: 於是吏士饥渴，人马甚疲，且夜至，又无堑垒。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers were thirsty and hungry, men and horses very weary, and moreover arrived at night, and moreover had no moats or ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The attackers arrived famished and parched at midnight, with no trenches or palisades to shelter them.

sentences.zh: 释甲休息，而布又宣言相惊，云「城中贼出来」。

translations.literal: They removed armor and rested, but Bu again declared words to alarm each other, saying, “The bandits in the city have come out.”
translations.idiomatic: They shed their armor to rest, until Lü Bu’s men raised another false cry that “the enemy is sallying from the town.”

sentences.zh: 军众扰乱奔走，皆弃甲，失鞍马。

translations.literal: The army masses were thrown into confusion and ran; all abandoned armor and lost saddles and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The host dissolved in panic, casting off mail and losing mounts in the rout.

sentences.zh: 行十餘里，定无贼，会天明，便还，拾取兵器，欲进攻城。

translations.literal: After proceeding more than ten li, determining there were no bandits, it happened to be dawn; they then returned, picked up weapons, and wished to advance and attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: They fled several li before realizing no enemy was behind them; at daybreak they straggled back, gathered their arms, and prepared to renew the assault.

sentences.zh: 城守已固，穿堑已深，轸等不能攻而还。〉

translations.literal: City defenses were already solid, moats dug already deep; Zhen and the others could not attack and returned.〉
translations.idiomatic: By then the walls were manned and the ditches deep; Hu Zhen had no choice but to withdraw.〉

sentences.zh: 堅移屯梁東，大為卓軍所攻，堅與數十騎潰圍而出。

translations.literal: Jian shifted encampment east of Liang and was greatly attacked by Zhuo’s army; Jian with several tens of cavalry broke the encirclement and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian moved his camp east of Liang, where Dong Zhuo’s army fell on him in force; he cut his way out with only a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 堅常著赤罽幘，乃脫幘令親近將祖茂著之。

translations.literal: Jian constantly wore a red wool turban; thereupon he removed the turban and ordered his intimate general Zu Mao to wear it.
translations.idiomatic: He always fought in his trademark crimson wool cap; he pulled it off and pressed it on his trusted officer Zu Mao.

sentences.zh: 卓騎爭逐茂，故堅從間道得免。

translations.literal: Zhuo’s cavalry vied to pursue Mao; therefore Jian by a bypath was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo’s riders swarmed after the red cap, which let Sun Jian slip away down a side path.

sentences.zh: 茂困迫，下馬，以幘冠塚閒燒柱，因伏草中。

translations.literal: Mao, pressed to extremity, dismounted, placed the turban on a burned pillar among the tombs, and thereupon lay hidden in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Mao, cornered, leaped down, perched the cap on a charred grave-marker, and flattened himself in the weeds.

sentences.zh: 卓騎望見，圍繞數重，定近覺是柱，乃去。

translations.literal: Zhuo’s cavalry, seeing from afar, surrounded several layers; when they drew near and realized it was a pillar, they left.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers ringed the spot in tight circles until they saw it was only a post, then rode off.

sentences.zh: 堅復相收兵，合戰於陽人，大破卓軍，梟其都督華雄等。

translations.literal: Jian again gathered troops, joined battle at Yangren, greatly defeated Zhuo’s army, and displayed the heads of their overseer Hua Xiong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian rallied his men, met Dong Zhuo’s army again at Yangren, shattered it, and took the head of commander Hua Xiong among others.

sentences.zh: 是時，或間堅於術，術懷疑，不運軍糧。

translations.literal: At that time someone slandered Jian to Shu; Shu harbored suspicion and did not transport military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Someone whispered poison into Yuan Shu’s ear; Yuan Shu began to doubt him and cut off the grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：或谓术曰：「坚若得洛，不可复制，此为除狼而得虎也」，故术疑之。〉

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Someone said to Shu, “If Jian takes Luoyang, he can no longer be controlled—this is removing a wolf and getting a tiger”; therefore Shu suspected him.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan quotes a warning to Yuan Shu: “Let Sun Jian seize Luoyang and you will never leash him again—you trade a wolf for a tiger,” which fed Yuan Shu’s suspicions.〉

sentences.zh: 陽人去魯陽百餘里，堅夜馳見術，畫地計校，曰：「所以出身不顧，上為國家討賊，下慰將軍家門之私仇。

translations.literal: Yangren is more than a hundred li from Luyang; Jian by night galloped to see Shu, drew on the ground to calculate, and said, “The reason I have left myself without regard is above for the state punishing the bandit, below to console Your General’s family’s private enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Yangren lies a hundred-odd li from Luyang; Sun Jian rode through the night to Yuan Shu, traced lines in the dust as he argued, and said, “I risked everything to serve the throne against a traitor and to avenge your own family feud.

sentences.zh: 堅與卓非有骨肉之怨也，而將軍受譖潤之言，還相嫌疑！」

translations.literal: Jian and Zhuo do not have the enmity of flesh and bone, yet Your General, receiving slanderous moist words, in return mutually suspects!”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian and Dong Zhuo are no blood enemies—yet you swallow gossip and turn on your ally!”

sentences.zh: 〈《江表传》载坚语曰：「大勋垂捷而军粮不继，此吴起所以叹泣於西河，乐毅所以遗恨於垂成也。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan records Jian’s words, saying, “A great merit hangs on the verge of success yet army grain does not follow—this is why Wu Qi wept west of the river, and why Yue Yi left regret at the verge of completion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan gives his fuller speech: “Victory is within reach and the supplies stop—this is Wu Qi weeping west of the River, this is Yue Yi’s regret on the brink of triumph.

sentences.zh: 原将军深思之。」〉

translations.literal: I beg the General to think deeply on this.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Think hard on that, General.”〉

sentences.zh: 術踧踖，即調發軍糧。

translations.literal: Shu was uneasy; at once he transferred and issued military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu squirmed, then ordered the grain released at once.

sentences.zh: 堅還屯。

translations.literal: Jian returned to encamp.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian rode back to his camp.

sentences.zh: 卓憚堅猛壯，乃遣將軍李傕等來求和親。

translations.literal: Zhuo feared Jian’s fierceness and strength; thereupon he sent Generals Li Jue and others to come seek peace by marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo, unnerved by Sun Jian’s ferocity, sent Li Jue and others to propose a marriage pact.

sentences.zh: 令堅列疏子弟任刺史、郡守者，許表用之。

translations.literal: He ordered Jian to list in a memorial sons and younger brothers who held posts as Inspector or Grand Administrator, promising to memorialize their appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Sun Jian to register any relatives who might serve as inspectors or grand administrators, promising imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「卓逆天無道，蕩覆王室。

translations.literal: Jian said, “Zhuo opposes Heaven and is without the Way; he has overturned the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian replied, “Dong Zhuo defies Heaven and the moral order; he has wrecked the Han.

sentences.zh: 今不夷汝三族，懸示四海，則吾死不瞑目。

translations.literal: If now I do not exterminate your three clans and hang your heads to display to the four seas, then when I die I will not close my eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Unless I wipe out his three lineages and stake his heads for the realm to see, I shall not rest in my grave.

sentences.zh: 豈將與乃和親邪？

translations.literal: Could I possibly make peace and marriage alliance with you?”
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine I would treat with him?”

sentences.zh: 」復進軍大谷。

translations.literal: Again he advanced the army to Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed his host on toward the Dagu pass.

sentences.zh: 拒雒九十里。

translations.literal: He resisted Luoyang at ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: His front stood ninety li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 〈山阳公载记曰：卓谓长史刘艾曰：「关东军败数矣，皆畏孤，无能为也。

translations.literal: The Shanyang Gong Zaiji states: Zhuo said to Chief Clerk Liu Ai, “The east-of-the-mountain army has been defeated several times; all fear me and can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang Gong Zaiji records Dong Zhuo telling Chief Clerk Liu Ai, “The coalition east of the mountains has lost again and again; they are terrified of me and can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟孙坚小戆，颇能用人，当语诸将，使知忌之。

translations.literal: Only Sun Jian is a little foolish, yet is rather able to employ men; I ought to tell the various generals to make them know to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Jian is a stubborn fool, but he knows how to use men—you should warn our generals to beware of him.

sentences.zh: 孤昔与周慎西征，慎围边、韩於金城。

translations.literal: In the past I with Zhou Shen campaigned west; Shen besieged Bian and Han at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Shen and I marched west together: Shen pinned Bian Zhang and Han Sui inside Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 孤语张温，求引所将兵为慎作后驻。

translations.literal: I spoke to Zhang Wen, asking to lead the troops I commanded to be Shen’s rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: I begged Zhang Wen to let me bring up the rear with my own command.

sentences.zh: 温不听。

translations.literal: Wen did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 孤时上言其形势，知慎必不克。

translations.literal: I at the time upward spoke on the situation, knowing Shen certainly could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: I memorialized then on how the lines stood—I knew Shen could not win.

sentences.zh: 台今有本末。

translations.literal: The court now has the beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: The court archives still hold the whole sequence of those memorials.

sentences.zh: 事未报，温又使孤讨先零叛羌，以为西方可一时荡定。

translations.literal: The matter had not yet been answered when Wen again ordered me to punish the Xianling rebel Qiang, thinking the west could in one stroke be swept settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before any reply came, Zhang Wen ordered me west again against the Xianling Qiang, sure the region could be pacified at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 孤皆知其不然而不得止，遂行，留别部司马刘靖将步骑四千屯安定，以为声势。

translations.literal: I all knew it was not so but could not stop it; thereupon I marched, leaving Adjutant Liu Jing of a separate division to lead four thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Anding to make a show of force.
translations.idiomatic: I knew it was folly but had to go; I left Adjutant Liu Jing with four thousand horse and foot at Anding as a feint.

sentences.zh: 叛羌便还，欲截归道，孤小击辄开，畏安定有兵故也。

translations.literal: The rebel Qiang then returned, wishing to cut the return road; I with a small strike then opened them, because they feared Anding had troops.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous Qiang tried to block our retreat until I hit them lightly and broke the trap—they still feared Liu Jing at Anding.

sentences.zh: 虏谓安定当数万人，不知但靖也。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought Anding ought to have tens of thousands of men, not knowing there was only Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They assumed Anding held a host in strength, never guessing it was only Liu Jing’s detachment.

sentences.zh: 时又上章言状，而孙坚随周慎行，谓慎求将万兵造金城，使慎以二万作后驻，边、韩城中无宿谷，当於外运，畏慎大兵，不敢轻与坚战，而坚兵足以断其运道，兒曹用必还羌谷中，凉州或能定也。

translations.literal: At that time again upward memorialized stating the situation, while Sun Jian followed Zhou Shen’s march, said to Shen asking to lead ten thousand troops to advance on Jincheng, making Shen use twenty thousand as rear station; Bian and Han inside the city had no stored grain, had to transport from outside; fearing Shen’s great army, they would not dare lightly join battle with Jian, while Jian’s troops sufficed to cut their supply routes; those wretches would certainly return to Qiang valleys; Liangzhou perhaps could be settled.
translations.idiomatic: I sent another memorial laying out the map: Sun Jian was marching with Zhou Shen and urged him to detach ten thousand men to press Jincheng while Shen kept twenty thousand in reserve. Bian Zhang and Han Sui had no granaries inside the walls and had to haul grain from outside. They would flinch from Shen’s main body and would not dare meet Sun Jian lightly, yet Jian’s corps could choke their convoys—those rabble would be driven back into the Qiang hills, and Liangzhou might yet be brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 温既不能用孤，慎又不用坚，自攻金城，坏其外垣，驰使语温，自以克在旦夕，温时亦自以计中也。

translations.literal: Wen was already unable to employ me, and Shen again did not employ Jian; he himself attacked Jincheng, destroyed its outer wall, and galloped a messenger to tell Wen, himself thinking capture was at dawn and dusk; Wen at the time also himself thought the plan had hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen would not use me, and Zhou Shen spurned Sun Jian’s plan: Shen stormed Jincheng himself, broke the outer rampart, and sent couriers boasting that victory was a matter of hours—Zhang Wen thought the trap had sprung shut.

sentences.zh: 而渡辽兒果断

translations.literal: But the “sons who crossed the Liao” acted with decision
translations.idiomatic: Then the Wuhuan auxiliaries from beyond the Liao struck their blow

sentences.zh: （蔡园）

translations.literal: (marginal variant: “Cai Garden”)
translations.idiomatic: (Manuscript gloss: “Cai Garden.”)

sentences.zh: 〔葵园〕，慎弃辎重走，果如孤策。

translations.literal: [Textual variant “Kuai Garden”:] Shen abandoned heavy baggage and fled; it turned out as I had calculated.〉
translations.idiomatic: [Alternate reading “Kuai Garden”: Zhou Shen threw away his baggage train and ran—exactly as I had predicted.〉

sentences.zh: 台以此封孤都乡侯。

translations.literal: The court for this enfeoffed me Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On that account the court invested me as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 坚以佐军司马，所见与人同，自为可耳。

translations.literal: Jian, as assistant army major, what he saw was the same as other people; he himself thought it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian was only an assistant army major, yet he read the field the same way I did and believed his counsel sound.

sentences.zh: 」艾曰：「坚虽时见计，故自不如李傕、郭汜。

translations.literal: ” Ai said, “Although Jian at times saw stratagems, in the end he is not the match of Li Jue and Guo Si.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ai answered, “Sun Jian may have flashes of insight, but he is still no Li Jue or Guo Si.

sentences.zh: 闻在美阳亭北，将千骑步与虏合，殆死，亡失印绶，此不为能也。

translations.literal: I heard north of Meiyang Pavilion he led a thousand cavalry and infantry and joined the barbarians in battle, nearly died, lost seals and ribbons—this is not being capable.”
translations.idiomatic: They say north of Meiyang Pavilion he took a thousand mixed troops against the Qiang, nearly died, and lost his seals of office—that is hardly genius.”

sentences.zh: 」卓曰：「坚时乌合义从，兵不如虏精，且战有利钝。

translations.literal: ” Zhuo said, “Jian at the time was a motley host of righteous followers; troops were not as refined as the barbarians’, and moreover in battle there are sharp and dull.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo retorted, “Sun Jian then led a scratch militia, not elite like the Qiang, and every battle has its good and bad days.

sentences.zh: 但当论山东大势，终无所至耳。

translations.literal: One ought only to discuss the great situation east of the mountains; in the end they will arrive nowhere.”
translations.idiomatic: Judge the larger picture east of the mountains—they will never get here.”

sentences.zh: 」艾曰：「山东兒驱略百姓，以作寇逆，其锋不如人，坚甲利兵强弩之用又不如人，亦安得久？

translations.literal: ” Ai said, “The sons east of the mountains drive and plunder common people to make rebellion and inversion; their edge is not as good as others; in the use of stout armor, sharp weapons, and strong crossbows they are again not as good as others—how can they long endure?”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ai said, “Those easterners live by raiding the people; their edge is dull, their armor and crossbows inferior—how long can that last?”

sentences.zh: 」卓曰：「然，但杀二袁、刘表、孙坚，天下自服从孤耳。」〉

translations.literal: ” Zhuo said, “So it is; only kill the two Yuans, Liu Biao, and Sun Jian, and the realm will of itself submit and obey me.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo answered, “True—kill the two Yuans, Liu Biao, and Sun Jian, and the world kneels to me.”〉

sentences.zh: 卓尋徙都西入關，焚燒雒邑。

translations.literal: Zhuo before long moved the capital west and entered the passes, burning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dong Zhuo abandoned Luoyang, withdrew into the passes, and put the capital to the torch.

sentences.zh: 堅乃前入至雒，修諸陵，平塞卓所發掘。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon advanced and entered to Luoyang, repaired the various tombs, leveled and blocked what Zhuo had dug up.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pressed into Luoyang, restored the imperial tombs, and refilled the graves Dong Zhuo had opened.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：旧京空虚，数百里中无烟火。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: The old capital was empty; within several hundred li there was no cooking smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says the ancient capital lay deserted, with no hearth smoke for a hundred li around.

sentences.zh: 坚前入城，惆怅流涕。

translations.literal: When Jian advanced and entered the city, he was melancholy and wept tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian walked those streets he wept for the ruin of the city.

sentences.zh: 吴书曰：坚入洛，扫除汉宗庙，祠以太牢。

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: When Jian entered Luoyang, he swept the Han ancestral shrines and sacrificed with the grand ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records that he swept the Han shrines and offered the highest grade of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 坚军城南甄官井上，旦有五色气，举军惊怪，莫有敢汲。

translations.literal: Jian’s army was south of the city at the Zhenguan Well; at dawn there was five-colored qi; the whole army was startled and wondered, and none dared draw water.
translations.idiomatic: His camp stood south of town over the Zhenguan Well; at dawn five-colored vapors rose, and the whole army shrank from touching the water.

sentences.zh: 坚令人入井，探得汉传国玺，文曰「受命于天，既寿永昌」，方圜四寸，上纽交五龙，上一角缺。

translations.literal: Jian ordered a man to enter the well, explore, and obtain the Han transmission seal of state; the inscription read “Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and prosperous stability”; square and round four cun; on the knob intertwined five dragons; on top one horn was missing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a man down the shaft and brought up the Han heirloom jade seal, carved “Ordered by Heaven; long life and glory steadfast,” four cun across, its knob wound with five dragons and one horn chipped away.

sentences.zh: 初，黄门张让等作乱，劫天子出奔，左右分散，掌玺者以投井中。

translations.literal: In the beginning, the Yellow Gates Zhang Rang and others made rebellion, seized the Son of Heaven and fled; those at his side scattered, and the one who held the seal cast it into the well.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Zhang Rang and his clique kidnapped the emperor and fled, the seal-bearer flung it into that well.

sentences.zh: 《山阳公载记》曰：袁术将僭号，闻坚得传国玺，乃拘坚夫人而夺之。

translations.literal: The Shanyang Gong Zaiji states: Yuan Shu was about to usurp the title; hearing Jian obtained the transmission seal of state, thereupon he seized Jian’s wife and took it from her.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang Gong Zaiji adds that Yuan Shu, plotting to declare himself emperor, imprisoned Sun Jian’s wife until she surrendered the seal.

sentences.zh: 江表传曰：案汉献帝起居注云「天子从河上还，得六玺於阁上」，又太康之初孙皓送金玺六枚，无有玉，明其伪也。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: According to the Han Xiandi Qiju Zhu it says “When the Son of Heaven returned from the River, he obtained six seals on the pavilion,” and moreover at the beginning of Taikang Sun Hao sent six gold seals, among which there was no jade, clarifying that it was false.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan cites Emperor Xian’s diary—“six seals were recovered from the gallery when the court came back from the river”—and notes that when Sun Hao surrendered at the start of the Jin he handed over six gold seals, none of jade, which proves the tale false.

sentences.zh: 虞喜《志林》曰：天子六玺者，文曰「皇帝之玺」、「皇帝行玺」、「皇帝信玺」、「天子之玺」、「天子行玺」、「天子信玺」。

translations.literal: Yu Xi’s Zhi Lin states: The Son of Heaven’s six seals: the inscriptions read “Seal of the Emperor,” “Seal of the Emperor for travel,” “Seal of the Emperor for trust,” “Seal of the Son of Heaven,” “Seal of the Son of Heaven for travel,” “Seal of the Son of Heaven for trust.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi’s Zhi Lin lists the six imperial chops: “Emperor’s seal,” “Emperor’s traveling seal,” “Emperor’s credential seal,” “Son of Heaven’s seal,” “Son of Heaven’s traveling seal,” and “Son of Heaven’s credential seal.”

sentences.zh: 此六玺所封事异，故文字不同。

translations.literal: These six seals seal different matters; therefore the characters are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Each served a different function, hence the differing legends on the faces.

sentences.zh: 《献帝起注》云「从河上还，得六玉玺於阁上」，此之谓也。

translations.literal: The Xian Di Qi Zhu states “Returning from the River, obtained six jade seals on the pavilion”; this is what it refers to.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian Emperor’s diary speaks of “six jade seals recovered from the gallery”—that is the set Yu Xi means.

sentences.zh: 传国玺者，乃汉高祖所佩秦皇帝玺，世世传受，号曰传国玺。

translations.literal: The transmission seal of state is the seal of the Qin Emperor worn by Han Gaozu; generation after generation it was transmitted and received, titled the transmission seal of state.
translations.idiomatic: The heirloom seal was the Qin emperor’s chop passed down to Han Gaozu—the fabled “transmission seal” handed from ruler to ruler.

sentences.zh: 案传国玺不在六玺之数，安得总其说乎？

translations.literal: According to the transmission seal of state is not within the number of the six seals; how can one lump together their explanations?
translations.idiomatic: That heirloom lies outside the six-office set; conflating the two traditions only breeds confusion.

sentences.zh: 应氏《汉官》、皇甫《世纪》，其论六玺，文义皆符。

translations.literal: Ying’s Han Guan and Huangfu’s Shiji, in their discussions of the six seals, the text and meaning all match.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao’s Han offices treatise and Huangfu Mi’s chronicle both describe the six seals in matching terms.

sentences.zh: 汉宫传国玺，文曰「受命于天，既寿且康」。

translations.literal: The Han palace transmission seal of state inscription reads “Receiving the mandate from Heaven, long life and moreover peace.”
translations.idiomatic: The Han court’s own record of the heirloom reads “Ordered by Heaven; long life and, moreover, peace.”

sentences.zh: 「且康」「永昌」，二字为错，未知两家何者为得。

translations.literal: “Moreover peace” and “prosperous stability,” two characters are transposed; it is not known which of the two families is correct.
translations.idiomatic: “And peace” versus “ever flourishing”—two characters differ, and which manuscript is right remains unclear.

sentences.zh: 金玉之精，率有光气，加以神器秘宝，辉耀益彰，盖一代之奇观，将来之异闻，而以不解之故，强谓之伪，不亦诬乎！

translations.literal: The essence of gold and jade generally has light and qi; adding the divine vessel’s secret treasure, its radiance shines still more clearly; it is a marvel of a generation, a strange report for the future, yet because of not understanding the reason, forcibly calling it false—is this not slander?
translations.idiomatic: Gold and jade naturally glow; a sacred relic shines all the brighter. To dismiss a wonder of the age as forgery, simply because the texts do not line up, is calumny.

sentences.zh: 陈寿为破虏传亦除此说，俱惑《起居注》，不知六玺殊名，与传国为七者也。

translations.literal: Chen Shou for the biography of Who Smashes the Caitiffs also removed this theory, both deluded by the Qiju Zhu, not knowing the six seals have different names, and with the transmission seal make seven.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou dropped the story from Sun Jian’s biography because he trusted the diary entry without noticing that six routine seals plus the heirloom make seven distinct pieces.

sentences.zh: 吴时无能刻玉，故天子以金为玺。

translations.literal: In Wu times there was no ability to carve jade; therefore the Son of Heaven used gold for seals.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu lacked craftsmen who could carve jade, so its emperors used gold seals instead.

sentences.zh: 玺虽以金，於文不异。

translations.literal: Although the seal used gold, in the inscription there was no difference.
translations.idiomatic: The metal changed, but the inscription remained the same.

sentences.zh: 吴降而送玺者送天子六玺，曩所得玉玺，乃古人遗印，不可施用。

translations.literal: When Wu surrendered and the one who sent seals sent the Son of Heaven’s six seals, the jade seal obtained long ago was an ancient person’s left-behind seal and could not be applied in use.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu capitulated it handed over the six routine chops; the jade piece Sun Jian was said to have found was only an antique keepsake, not usable as the dynastic seal.

sentences.zh: 天子之玺，今以无有为难，不通其义者耳。

translations.literal: As for the Son of Heaven’s seals, now taking nonexistence as difficulty is not comprehending its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: To insist the heirloom “cannot exist” because one copy is missing is to miss the point entirely.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为孙坚於兴义之中最有忠烈之称，若得汉神器而潜匿不言，此为阴怀异志，岂所谓忠臣者乎？

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that Sun Jian amid raising righteousness had the title of foremost loyal fierceness; if he obtained the Han divine vessel and secretly concealed it without speaking, this is harboring a different intent in the dark—how can this be called a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: I, Pei Songzhi, hold that Sun Jian won fame as the most gallant loyalist of the coalition: had he truly stolen the Han regalia and hidden it, he would have been a traitor in his heart, not the faithful servant the histories praise.

sentences.zh: 吴史欲以为国华，而不知损坚之令德。

translations.literal: The Wu histories wished to take it as a splendor of the state, but did not know it injures Jian’s fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wu chroniclers turned the tale into a national treasure story, unaware that it tarnishes Sun Jian’s good name.

sentences.zh: 如其果然，以传子孙，纵非六玺之数，要非常人所畜，孙皓之降，亦不得但送六玺，而宝藏传国也。

translations.literal: If it were indeed so, to transmit to sons and grandsons, even if not within the number of the six seals, in the end it is not what ordinary people hoard; at Sun Hao’s surrender, also he could not but send six seals, yet treasure-hoard the transmission seal.
translations.idiomatic: Had the seal been real and passed down in the family, it would not be an object common mortals could hide: when Sun Hao yielded he could not have sent only six chops while secreting the heirloom.

sentences.zh: 受命于天，奚取於归命之堂，若如喜言，则此玺今尚在孙门。

translations.literal: “Receiving the mandate from Heaven”—what is taken from the Hall of Surrendered Destiny; if like Xi’s words, then this seal today would still be in the Sun household.
translations.idiomatic: The motto “Ordered by Heaven” belongs on the Jin’s “Submission” plaque; if Yu Xi were right, that jade would still sit in Sun Jian’s line.

sentences.zh: 匹夫怀璧，犹曰有罪，而况斯物哉！〉

translations.literal: A common man cherishing a jade disk is still said to have guilt—how much the more this object!〉
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says a commoner who clutches a jade invites disaster—how much worse for a prize like that!〉

sentences.zh: 訖，引軍還，住魯陽。

translations.literal: When finished, he led the army back and halted at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he withdrew his army and camped again at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：是时关东州郡，务相兼并以自强大。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: At that time the provinces and commanderies east of the mountain strove with one another to annex and thereby strengthen themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu observes that east of the mountains every warlord swallowed his neighbor to grow strong.

sentences.zh: 袁绍遣会稽周喁为豫州刺史，来袭取州。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao dispatched Zhou You of Kuaiji as Inspector of Yuzhou, coming to attack and seize the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao appointed Zhou You of Kuaiji as inspector of Yuzhou and sent him to wrest the province from Sun Jian.

sentences.zh: 坚慨然叹曰：「同举义兵，将救社稷。

translations.literal: Jian sighed with feeling and said, “Together we raised righteous troops intending to rescue the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian said with a bitter sigh, “We rose together to save the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 逆贼垂破而各若此，吾当谁与戮力乎！

translations.literal: The rebellious bandit hangs on the verge of destruction, yet each is like this—with whom shall I join strength!”
translations.idiomatic: The traitor is nearly broken, yet here we are clawing at each other—who is left for me to fight beside?”

sentences.zh: 」言发涕下。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off in tears.

sentences.zh: 喁字仁明，周昕之弟也。

translations.literal: You’s courtesy name was Renming; he was the younger brother of Zhou Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou You, courtesy Renming, was Zhou Xin’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 《会稽典录》曰：初曹公兴义兵，遣人要喁，喁即收合兵众，得二千人，从公征伐，以为军师。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji Dianlu states: In the beginning when Lord Cao raised righteous troops, he sent someone to invite You; You at once gathered troops and masses, obtained two thousand men, followed the lord on campaign, and was made army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji Dianlu records that when Cao Cao first raised his loyal army he summoned Zhou You, who mustered two thousand men, marched with him, and served as strategist.

sentences.zh: 后与坚争豫州，屡战失利。

translations.literal: Later he contended with Jian for Yuzhou and repeatedly fought to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fought Sun Jian for Yuzhou and lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 会次兄九江太守昂为袁术所攻，喁往助之。

translations.literal: It happened that his next elder brother Ang, Grand Administrator of Jiujiang, was attacked by Yuan Shu, and You went to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Zhou Ang, prefect of Jiujiang, came under Yuan Shu’s attack, Zhou You rode to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 军败，还乡里，为许贡所害。〉

translations.literal: The army was defeated; returning to his home region, he was killed by Xu Gong.〉
translations.idiomatic: His force was shattered; on his way home Xu Gong murdered him.〉

sentences.zh: 初平三年，術使堅征荊州，擊劉表。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuping, Shu ordered Jian to campaign against Jingzhou and strike Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping 3 (192) Yuan Shu ordered Sun Jian to invade Jingzhou and bring Liu Biao to battle.

sentences.zh: 表遣黃祖逆於樊、鄧之間。

translations.literal: Biao sent Huang Zu to oppose him between Fan and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent Huang Zu to intercept him between Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 堅擊破之，追渡漢水，遂圍襄陽，單馬行峴山，為祖軍士所射殺。

translations.literal: Jian defeated him, pursued across the Han River, thereupon besieged Xiangyang, and riding a single horse on Xian Mountain was shot and killed by Zu’s soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian routed him, crossed the Han in pursuit, and laid siege to Xiangyang; riding alone on Xian Mountain he was cut down by Huang Zu’s archers.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰；

translations.literal: The Dianlüe states as follows:
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe gives this account:

sentences.zh: 坚悉其众攻表，表闭门，夜遣将黄祖潜出发兵。

translations.literal: Jian used all his host to attack Biao; Biao closed the gates and by night sent General Huang Zu secretly to lead troops out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian threw his whole army against Liu Biao, who barred the gates and slipped Huang Zu out by night with a relief column.

sentences.zh: 祖将兵欲还，坚逆与战。

translations.literal: Zu was leading troops wishing to return; Jian opposed him and joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: As Huang Zu tried to withdraw, Sun Jian intercepted and attacked.

sentences.zh: 祖败走，窜岘山中。

translations.literal: Zu fled defeated and bolted into Xian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu broke and fled into the Xian hills.

sentences.zh: 坚乘胜夜追祖，祖部兵从竹木间暗射坚，杀之。

translations.literal: Jian by night pursued Zu with victory; Zu’s troops from among bamboo and trees in the dark shot Jian and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pressed the pursuit through the night; Huang Zu’s men ambushed him from the bamboo groves and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：坚时年三十七。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: Jian at that time was thirty-seven sui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu gives his age as thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 英雄记曰：坚以初平四年正月七日死。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji states: Jian died on the seventh day of the first month of the fourth year of Chuping.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji dates his death to the seventh day of the first month, Chuping 4 (193).

sentences.zh: 又云：刘表将吕公将兵缘山向坚，坚轻骑寻山讨公。

translations.literal: It also says: Liu Biao’s general Lü Gong led troops along the mountain toward Jian; Jian with light cavalry sought along the mountain to punish Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Another version names Liu Biao’s officer Lü Gong, who moved along the ridge against Sun Jian while Sun Jian took light horse to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 公兵下石。

translations.literal: Gong’s soldiers rolled stones downward.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gong’s men rolled rocks down the slope.

sentences.zh: 中坚头，应时脑出物故。

translations.literal: They struck Jian’s head; on the spot his brains came out and he died.
translations.idiomatic: A stone struck Sun Jian’s head; his brains spilled out and he died instantly.

sentences.zh: 其不同如此也。〉

translations.literal: Their dissimilarity is thus.〉
translations.idiomatic: The accounts diverge in just this way.〉

sentences.zh: 兄子賁，帥將士眾就術。

translations.literal: His elder brother’s son Ben led generals and soldiers and masses to join Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Sun Ben gathered the command and went over to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術復表賁為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu again memorialized asking that Ben be Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu again petitioned to name Sun Ben inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 堅四子：策、權、翊、匡。

translations.literal: Jian had four sons: Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian left four sons—Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang.

sentences.zh: 權既稱尊號，謚堅曰武烈皇帝。

translations.literal: When Quan had already assumed the honored title, he posthumously titled Jian Emperor Wu Lie.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan took the throne he canonized his father as Emperor Wu Lie.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：尊坚庙曰始祖，墓曰高陵。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: They honored Jian’s temple as First Ancestor and his tomb as Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu records that Sun Jian’s shrine was styled First Ancestor and his mausoleum Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 志林曰：坚有五子：策、权、翊、匡，吴氏所生；

translations.literal: The Zhi Lin states: Jian had five sons—Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang, born of Lady Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Pei’s Zhi Lin counts five sons—Ce, Quan, Yi, and Kuang, all born to Lady Wu;

sentences.zh: 少子朗，庶生也，一名仁。〉

translations.literal: the youngest son Lang was born of a concubine and also bore the name Ren.〉
translations.idiomatic: and a younger son, Lang, born to a concubine, who was also called Ren.〉

sentences.zh: 策字伯符。

translations.literal: Ce’s courtesy name was Bofu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce bore the courtesy name Bofu.

sentences.zh: 堅初興義兵，策將母徙居舒。

translations.literal: When Jian first raised righteous troops, Ce led his mother to move residence to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian first raised the loyal army, Sun Ce escorted his mother to settle at Shu.

sentences.zh: 與周瑜相友，收合士大夫，江、淮間人咸向之。

translations.literal: He befriended Zhou Yu, gathered scholars and officials, and people between the Yangzi and Huai all turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Zhou Yu, drew in gentlemen from every quarter, and won the allegiance of the Huai–Yangzi region.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：坚为硃俊所表，为佐军，留家著寿春。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Jian was recommended by Zhu Jun and made assistant to the army; he left his family lodged at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan notes that Zhu Jun recommended Sun Jian as army adjutant and that the family stayed at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 策年十餘岁，已交结知名，声誉发闻。

translations.literal: Ce, aged over ten years, had already formed connections with the famous, and his reputation spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was out of his teens Sun Ce had already befriended noted men and his name was abroad.

sentences.zh: 有周瑜者，与策同年，亦英达夙成，闻策声闻，自舒来造焉。

translations.literal: There was a Zhou Yu, the same age as Ce, also outstanding and mature from youth; hearing Ce’s fame and reputation, he came from Shu to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu, his contemporary, was equally precocious; hearing Sun Ce’s repute he traveled from Shu to call on him.

sentences.zh: 便推结分好，义同断金，劝策徙居舒，策从之。〉

translations.literal: They at once formed a sworn friendship as close as metal severed in two, urged Ce to move residence to Shu, and Ce followed him.〉
translations.idiomatic: They swore brotherhood as firm as split metal, Zhou Yu persuaded him to move to Shu, and Sun Ce agreed.〉

sentences.zh: 堅薨，還葬曲阿。

translations.literal: When Jian died, they returned to bury him at Qu’e.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian’s death the family brought his body home for burial at Qu’e.

sentences.zh: 已乃渡江居江都。

translations.literal: Afterward they crossed the river and dwelt at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: They then crossed the Yangzi and settled at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书曰：策当嗣侯，让与弟匡。〉

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Ce ought to have inherited the marquisate but yielded it to his younger brother Kuang.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Sun Ce should have inherited the marquisate but ceded it to Sun Kuang.〉

sentences.zh: 壽春，術已據之，繇乃渡江治曲阿。

translations.literal: Shouchun—Shu had already occupied it—thereupon Yao crossed the river and administered Qu’e.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu held Shouchun, so Liu Yao crossed the river and set up his government at Qu’e.

sentences.zh: 時吳景尚在丹楊，策從兄賁又為丹揚都尉，繇至，皆迫逐之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Jing was still in Danyang, and Ce’s cousin Ben was again Danyang commandant; when Yao arrived, all were forced to flee them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing still controlled Danyang, and Sun Ben served as its commandant; when Liu Yao arrived he drove them both out.

sentences.zh: 景、賁退捨歷陽。

translations.literal: Jing and Ben withdrew and encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing and Sun Ben fell back to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 繇遣樊能、于麋東屯橫江津，張英屯當利口，以距術。

translations.literal: Yao sent Fan Neng and Yu Mi east to encamp at Hengjiang Ford, and Zhang Ying encamped at the mouth of Dangli, to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao posted Fan Neng and Yu Mi eastward at the Hengjiang crossing and Zhang Ying at Dangli mouth to block Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術自用故吏琅邪惠衢為揚州刺史，更以景為督軍中郎將，與賁共將兵擊英等，連年不克。

translations.literal: Shu personally used his former clerk Hui Qu of Langya as Inspector of Yangzhou, again made Jing supervising army zhonglang jiang, and with Ben jointly led troops to strike Ying and the others; for years they could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu appointed his old retainer Hui Qu from Langya as inspector of Yangzhou, restored Wu Jing as supervising colonel, and with Sun Ben besieged Zhang Ying’s line for years without success.

sentences.zh: 策乃說術，乞助景等平定江東。

translations.literal: Ce thereupon persuaded Shu, begging to aid Jing and the others in pacifying Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce then talked Yuan Shu into letting him reinforce Wu Jing and win the east.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策说术云：「家有旧恩在东，原助舅讨横江；

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce persuaded Shu, saying, “The family has old kindness in the east; I wish to help my uncle attack Hengjiang;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan quotes him: “We still have friends east of the river—I want to help my uncle take the Hengjiang line;

sentences.zh: 横江拔，因投本土召募，可得三万兵，以佐明使君匡济汉室。

translations.literal: when Hengjiang is taken, I can then return to my native soil to recruit and can obtain thirty thousand troops to assist Your Enlightened Envoy in aiding the house of Han.”
translations.idiomatic: once that bridgehead falls I can go home, raise thirty thousand men, and help you restore the Han.”

sentences.zh: 」术知其恨，而以刘繇据曲阿，王朗在会稽，谓策未必能定，故许之。〉

translations.literal: Shu knew his resentment, but because Liu Yao held Qu’e and Wang Lang was in Kuaiji, he judged that Ce might not be able to settle the matter, and therefore granted permission.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu knew Sun Ce nursed a grudge, yet with Liu Yao dug in at Qu’e and Wang Lang in Kuaiji he gambled that the young commander could not finish the job—and said yes.〉

sentences.zh: 術表策為折沖校尉，行殄寇將軍，兵財千餘，騎數十匹，賓客願從者數百人。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized asking that Ce be Colonel Who Breaks the Charge and acting General Who Exterminates the Bandits, with military funds a bit over a thousand, several tens of horses, and several hundred retainers willing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu’s memorial named him Colonel Who Breaks the Charge and acting General Who Exterminates Bandits, with a thousand-odd cash, a few dozen mounts, and a few hundred volunteers.

sentences.zh: 比至歷陽，眾五六千。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Liyang, the host numbered five or six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Liyang he had five or six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 策母先自曲阿徙於歷陽，策又徙母阜陵，渡江轉鬥，所向皆破。

translations.literal: Ce’s mother had first moved from Qu’e to Liyang; Ce again moved his mother to Fuling, crossed the river, and turned to fight; wherever he faced, all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu had already shifted from Qu’e to Liyang; Sun Ce moved her again to Fuling, then crossed the river and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 莫敢當其鋒，而軍令整肅，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: None dared meet his edge, yet military orders were strict and awe-inspiring, and the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: No one could stand against his spearhead, yet his discipline was iron and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策渡江攻繇牛渚营，尽得邸阁粮谷、战具，是岁兴平二年也。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce crossed the river and attacked Yao’s Niuzhu camp, obtaining all the depot grain and war gear; that year was the second year of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan dates his storming of Liu Yao’s Niuzhu depot—seizing grain and ordnance—to Xingping 2 (195).

sentences.zh: 时彭城相薛礼、下邳相笮融依繇为盟主，礼据秣陵城，融屯县南。

translations.literal: At that time the Chancellor of Pengcheng Xue Li and the Chancellor of Xiapi Ze Rong relied on Yao as covenant lord; Li held Moling city, and Rong encamped south of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng chancellor Xue Li and Xiapi chancellor Ze Rong backed Liu Yao as league chief: Xue Li held Moling while Ze Rong camped south of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 策先攻融，融出兵交战，斩首五百餘级，融即闭门不敢动。

translations.literal: Ce first attacked Rong; Rong sent troops to join battle; more than five hundred heads were cut off; Rong thereupon closed the gates and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce struck Ze Rong first, killed five hundred in the field, and penned him inside his walls.

sentences.zh: 因渡江攻礼，礼突走，而樊能、于麋等复合众袭夺牛渚屯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed the river to attack Li; Li broke through and fled, while Fan Neng, Yu Mi, and others again combined masses to raid and seize the Niuzhu camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed to hit Xue Li, who bolted from Moling, while Fan Neng and Yu Mi rallied and snatched back the Niuzhu camp.

sentences.zh: 策闻之，还攻破能等，获男女万餘人。

translations.literal: When Ce heard it, he returned, defeated Neng and the others, and captured more than ten thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wheeled about, crushed Fan Neng’s force, and took ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 复下攻融，为流矢所中，伤股，不能乘马，因自舆还牛渚营。

translations.literal: He again advanced to attack Rong, was struck by a stray arrow, wounded in the thigh, could not ride a horse, and therefore in a litter himself returned to the Niuzhu camp.
translations.idiomatic: On his second push against Ze Rong a stray bolt wounded his thigh; unable to ride, he had himself carried back to Niuzhu in a litter.

sentences.zh: 或叛告融曰：「孙郎被箭已死。

translations.literal: Someone betraying informed Rong, saying, “Young Lord Sun has been struck by an arrow and is already dead.”
translations.idiomatic: A defector told Ze Rong, “The Young Commander is dead of his wound.”
