sentences.zh: 」融大喜，即遣将于兹乡策。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased and at once sent a general to Zi township to attack Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Rong rejoiced and sent a column to Zi township to finish Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策遣步骑数百挑战，设伏於后，贼出击之，锋刃未接而伪走，贼追入伏中，乃大破之，斩首千餘级。

translations.literal: Ce sent several hundred infantry and cavalry to challenge, set an ambush behind, and when the bandits came out to strike them, before blades met feigned flight; the bandits pursued into the ambush, and he thereupon greatly defeated them, cutting off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce baited him with a few hundred skirmishers, feigned flight into an ambush, and annihilated the sortie—over a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 策因往到融营下，令左右大呼曰：「孙郎竟云何！

translations.literal: Ce thereupon went to below Rong’s camp and ordered those at his sides to shout loudly, saying, “How indeed is Young Lord Sun!”
translations.idiomatic: He rode straight under Ze Rong’s walls and had his men bellow, “What news of the Young Commander now?”

sentences.zh: 」贼於是惊怖夜遁。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon were frightened and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison panicked and fled in the dark.

sentences.zh: 融闻策尚在，更深沟高垒，缮治守备。

translations.literal: Rong heard Ce was still alive, dug the moat deeper and raised the walls higher, and repaired defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze Rong learned Sun Ce still lived, he deepened his ditches, raised his ramparts, and rebuilt his defenses.

sentences.zh: 策以融所屯地势险固，乃舍去，攻破繇别将於海陵，转攻湖孰、江乘，皆下之。〉

translations.literal: Ce because the ground where Rong encamped was strategically dangerous and solid, therefore abandoned it and left, defeated Yao’s separate general at Hailing, turned to attack Huzhu and Jiangcheng, and took them all.〉
translations.idiomatic: Finding Ze Rong’s position too strong to rush, Sun Ce slipped away, crushed one of Liu Yao’s detachments at Hailing, then stormed Huzhu and Jiangcheng in turn.〉

sentences.zh: 策為人，美姿顔，好笑語，性闊達聽受，善於用人。

translations.literal: As a person Ce had handsome features, loved laughter and conversation, was by nature broad-minded and receptive, and was skilled at employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was striking to look at, quick to laugh, open-minded, and a natural leader of men.

sentences.zh: 是以士民見者，莫不盡心，樂為致死。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen and commoners who saw him, none did not give their whole hearts and were glad to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners alike gave him their hearts and would gladly die in his service.

sentences.zh: 劉繇棄軍遁逃，諸郡守皆捐城郭奔走。

translations.literal: Liu Yao abandoned the army and fled; the various grand administrators all cast aside cities and ramparts and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao threw away his army and ran; every magistrate abandoned his walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策时年少，虽有位号，而士民皆呼为孙郎。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce at the time was young; although he had rank and title, yet gentlemen and commoners all called him Young Lord Sun.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says that though Sun Ce already held rank, everyone called him “Young Lord Sun.”

sentences.zh: 百姓闻孙郎至，皆失魂魄；

translations.literal: The common people heard Young Lord Sun had arrived and all lost their souls;
translations.idiomatic: When word ran that Young Lord Sun was coming, folk were terrified;

sentences.zh: 长吏委城郭，窜伏山草。

translations.literal: long officials cast aside cities and ramparts and hid in mountain grass.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates bolted from their towns and cowered in the hills.

sentences.zh: 及至，军士奉令，不敢虏略，鸡犬菜茹，一无所犯，民乃大悦，竞以牛酒诣军。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the soldiers received orders and did not dare plunder; chickens, dogs, and garden vegetables—nothing was violated; the people thereupon were greatly pleased and vied to bring oxen and wine to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his troops obeyed orders to the letter—no looting, not a chicken or cabbage touched—and the people flocked with oxen and wine to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 刘繇既走，策入曲阿劳赐将士，遣将陈宝诣阜陵迎母及弟。

translations.literal: After Liu Yao had gone, Ce entered Qu’e, rewarded and feasted generals and soldiers, and sent General Chen Bao to Fuling to welcome his mother and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao’s flight Sun Ce entered Qu’e, feasted his army, and sent Chen Bao to Fuling to fetch his mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 发恩布令，告诸县：「其刘繇、笮融等故乡部曲来降首者，一无所问；

translations.literal: He issued kindness and spread orders, announcing to the counties: “As for native followers of Liu Yao, Ze Rong, and others who come to surrender first, nothing will be questioned;
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed across the counties: “Men who once served Liu Yao or Ze Rong may surrender without fear;

sentences.zh: 乐从军者，一身行，复除门户；

translations.literal: those glad to follow the army—one person enlists and his whole household is again exempted;
translations.idiomatic: those who enlist will have their entire household tax burden lifted;

sentences.zh: 不乐者，勿强也。

translations.literal: those not glad, do not force them.”
translations.idiomatic: those who decline will not be pressed.”

sentences.zh: 」旬日之间，四面云集，得见兵二万餘人，马千餘匹，威震江东，形势转盛。〉

translations.literal: Within ten days or so the four sides gathered like clouds; he could muster more than twenty thousand soldiers and over a thousand horses; his awe shook Jiangdong and the situation turned flourishing.〉
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days twenty thousand men and a thousand horses rallied to him, and his name shook the east.〉

sentences.zh: 吳人嚴白虎等眾各萬餘人，處處屯聚。

translations.literal: The Wu man Yan Baihu and others, each with hosts of over ten thousand, everywhere encamped and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Band chiefs such as Yan Baihu of Wu mustered ten thousand men apiece in strongholds across the land.

sentences.zh: 吳景等欲先擊破虎等，乃至會稽。

translations.literal: Wu Jing and the others wished first to attack and defeat Baihu and the others, and only then reach Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing wanted to crush Yan Baihu before marching on Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 策曰：「虎等群盜，非有大志，此成禽耳。

translations.literal: Ce said, “Baihu and the others are a pack of bandits; they do not harbor great ambitions—this is game already caged.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce answered, “Yan Baihu is only a hill bandit with no larger design—he is already in the net.”

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵渡浙江，據會稽，屠東冶，乃攻破虎等。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops across the Zhe River, seized Kuaiji, slaughtered Dongye, and thereupon defeated Baihu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Zhe, took Kuaiji, stormed Dongye, and broke Yan Baihu’s league.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴录》曰：时有乌程邹他、钱铜及前合浦太守嘉兴王晟等，各聚众万餘或数千。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu states: At that time in Wucheng Zou Ta, Qian Tong, and the former Grand Administrator of Hepu Wang Sheng of Jiaxing and others each gathered crowds of over ten thousand or several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu lists Wucheng’s Zou Ta and Qian Tong, ex-prefect of Hepu Wang Sheng of Jiaxing, and others, each with hosts in the thousands or tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 引兵扑讨，皆攻破之。

translations.literal: He led troops to strike and punish them and all defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce campaigned against each in turn and overthrew them.

sentences.zh: 策母吴氏曰：「晟与汝父有升堂见妻之分，今其诸子兄弟皆已枭夷，独餘一老翁，何足复惮乎？

translations.literal: Ce’s mother Lady Wu said, “Sheng with your father had the relationship of ascending the hall and seeing the wife; now his various sons and younger brothers have all been beheaded and displayed; only one old man remains—what is there again to fear?”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu said, “Wang Sheng was your father’s friend—he sat in our hall as family. His sons are dead; only the old man is left—why fear him?”

sentences.zh: 」乃舍之，餘咸族诛。

translations.literal: Thereupon she spared him; the rest were all executed by clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: She persuaded Sun Ce to spare Wang Sheng while the rest were extirpated to the last cousin.

sentences.zh: 策自讨虎，虎高垒坚守，使其弟舆请和。

translations.literal: Ce personally attacked Baihu; Baihu with high ramparts firmly defended and sent his younger brother Yu to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce besieged Yan Baihu, who held his high walls and sent his brother Yan Yu to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 许之。

translations.literal: He granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce agreed.

sentences.zh: 舆请独与策会面约。

translations.literal: Yu requested to meet Ce alone face to face to make a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yu asked for a private parley to seal the pact.

sentences.zh: 既会，策引白刃斫席，舆体动，策笑曰：「闻卿能坐跃，剿捷不常，聊戏卿耳！

translations.literal: After they met, Ce drew a white blade and chopped the mat; Yu’s body moved; Ce laughed and said, “I have heard you can leap from a seated position—your agility is not constant; I was merely jesting with you!”
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting Sun Ce slashed the mat with his sword; Yan Yu flinched, and Sun Ce laughed, “They say you can jump from a sitting start—I was only teasing.”

sentences.zh: 」舆曰：「我见刃乃然。

translations.literal: Yu said, “I only reacted thus when I saw the blade.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yu muttered, “Anyone would start at a naked blade.”

sentences.zh: 」策知其无能也，乃以手戟投之，立死。

translations.literal: Ce knew he lacked ability; thereupon with a hand halberd he cast at him, and he died standing.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the cowardice, Sun Ce hurled a short halberd and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 舆有勇力，虎众以其死也，甚惧。

translations.literal: Yu had courage and strength; Baihu’s crowd because of his death was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yu had been the band’s strongman; his death terrified Yan Baihu’s followers.

sentences.zh: 进攻破之。

translations.literal: He advanced, attacked, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce pressed the assault and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 虎奔餘杭，投许昭於虏中。

translations.literal: Baihu fled to Yuhang and threw himself to Xu Zhao in the midst of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Baihu fled to Yuhang and threw himself on Xu Zhao’s protection among the outlaws.

sentences.zh: 程普请击昭，策曰：「许昭有义於旧君，有诚於故友，此丈夫之志也。

translations.literal: Cheng Pu requested to strike Zhao; Ce said, “Xu Zhao has shown righteousness toward an old lord and sincerity toward an old friend—this is the aspiration of a great man.”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu urged an attack on Xu Zhao, but Sun Ce said, “He keeps faith with his old master and his old friends—that is the mark of a hero.”

sentences.zh: 」乃舍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he spared him.
translations.idiomatic: He let Xu Zhao be.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：许昭有义於旧君，谓济盛宪也，事见后注。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: as for “Xu Zhao has shown righteousness toward an old lord,” it refers to aiding Sheng Xian; the matter appears in a later note.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi glosses the “old lord” as Sheng Xian, whom Xu Zhao rescued—see the later commentary.

sentences.zh: 有诚於故友，则受严白虎也。〉

translations.literal: As for “sincerity toward an old friend,” it refers to receiving Yan Baihu.〉
translations.idiomatic: The “old friend” is Yan Baihu, whom he once harbored.〉

sentences.zh: 盡更置長吏，策自領會稽太守，復以吳景為丹楊太守，以孫賁為豫章太守，分豫章為廬陵郡，以賁弟輔為廬陵太守，丹揚朱治為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He completely replaced all long officials; Ce personally led as Grand Administrator of Kuaiji, again made Wu Jing Grand Administrator of Danyang, made Sun Ben Grand Administrator of Yuzhang, divided Yuzhang to make Luling commandery, made Ben’s younger brother Fu Grand Administrator of Luling, and Zhu Zhi of Danyang Grand Administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced every county magistrate, took Kuaiji himself, reappointed Wu Jing to Danyang, Sun Ben to Yuzhang, carved Luling out of Yuzhang for Sun Fu, and named Zhu Zhi prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 彭城張昭、廣陵張紘、秦松、陳端等，為謀主。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao of Pengcheng, Zhang Hong of Guangling, Qin Song, Chen Duan, and others were chief planners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao of Pengcheng, Zhang Hong of Guangling, Qin Song, and Chen Duan became his principal advisers.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策遣奉正都尉刘由、五官掾高承奉章诣许，拜献方物。〉

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce sent Rectification Colonel Liu You and Bureau Gentleman Gao Cheng bearing the memorial to Xu, bowing and presenting local products.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan records that he sent Liu You and Gao Cheng to the capital with tribute and a memorial of allegiance.〉

sentences.zh: 時袁術僭號，策以書責而絕之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shu usurped the title; Ce with a letter blamed him and broke relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu declared himself emperor, Sun Ce wrote to denounce him and severed their alliance.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴录》载策使张纮为书曰：「盖上天垂司过之星，圣王建敢谏之鼓，设非谬之备，急箴阙之言，何哉？

translations.literal: The Wu Lu records that Ce had Zhang Hong draft a letter, saying, “High Heaven hangs the star that oversees faults; sage kings set up the drum that welcomes blunt remonstrance; they prepare against error and falsehood and heed urgent admonition of gaps—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu preserves a letter drafted by Zhang Hong for Sun Ce: “Heaven posts a star to watch for misrule; the sage kings hung a drum for frank counsel—why, if not because every strength has its blind side?

sentences.zh: 凡有所长，必有所短也。

translations.literal: Whatever has a strength must also have a weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Power always walks with weakness.

sentences.zh: 去冬传有大计，无不悚惧；

translations.literal: Last winter word spread of a great plan; none were not fearful and trembling;
translations.idiomatic: Last winter rumors of your great design left everyone shaken;

sentences.zh: 旋知供备贡献，万夫解惑。

translations.literal: soon we learned you were only preparing tribute and submission, and ten thousand men set their doubts to rest.
translations.idiomatic: then we heard you were merely assembling tribute for the court, and a hundred thousand fears melted away.

sentences.zh: 顷闻建议，复欲追遵前图，即事之期，便有定月。

translations.literal: Recently I heard counsel advising you again to pursue and honor the former scheme; for the affair’s timing there is already a fixed month.
translations.idiomatic: Now fresh advice urges you back toward that throne—some even name the very month.

sentences.zh: 益使怃然，想是流妄；

translations.literal: It all the more makes one despondent; I suppose it is floating rumor;
translations.idiomatic: That rumor leaves us heartsick—I pray it is only idle talk;

sentences.zh: 设其必尔，民何望乎？

translations.literal: suppose it were indeed so—what could the people look to?
translations.idiomatic: but if it were true, what hope would the people have?

sentences.zh: 曩日之举义兵也，天下之士所以响应者，董卓擅废置，害太后、弘农王，略烝宫人，发掘园陵，暴逆至此，故诸州郡雄豪闻声慕义。

translations.literal: On the day we first raised the righteous army, the reason the empire’s gentlemen responded was that Dong Zhuo on his own authority deposed and installed rulers, murdered the empress dowager and Prince Hongnong, violated and carried off palace women, dug up imperial gardens and tombs, and his violence and treason reached this pitch—therefore the heroes of every province and commandery heard the call and yearned for the right.
translations.idiomatic: We took up arms because Dong Zhuo set aside emperors at will, killed the Dowager and the Prince of Hongnong, ravaged the harem, opened the imperial tombs, and outraged Heaven and earth—so every warlord rose for justice.

sentences.zh: 神武外振，卓遂内歼。

translations.literal: Divine martialness shook them from without, and Zhuo was thereupon destroyed within.
translations.idiomatic: Your might shattered him from without, and his own wickedness consumed him within.

sentences.zh: 元恶既毙，幼主东顾，俾保傅宣命，欲令诸军振旅，

translations.literal: The chief villain already dead, the young lord looks east; he has ordered tutors and guardians to proclaim commands, wishing to make the various armies pack their gear and return.
translations.idiomatic: The arch-rebel is dead; the boy emperor faces east again while his tutors issue edicts for every army to stack arms and go home.

translations.literal: (Marginal gloss: the character yú, “at/in.”)
translations.idiomatic: (Manuscript gloss: possibly insert yú, “at,” in the preceding clause.)

sentences.zh: 河北通谋黑山，曹操放毒东徐，刘表称乱南荆，公孙瓚炰烋北幽，刘繇决力江浒，刘备争盟淮隅，是以未获承命櫜弓戢戈也。

translations.literal: north of the River they plot with the Black Mountain band; Cao Cao poisons the eastern Xu region; Liu Biao stirs rebellion in southern Jing; Gongsun Zan rages in northern You; Liu Yao strains his strength along the river; Liu Bei vies for alliance on the Huai bends—therefore we have not yet been able to receive the command to sheathe bows and store spears.
translations.idiomatic: Yet north of the river the Black Mountain league plots with Yuan Shao, Cao Cao ravages Xu, Liu Biao seethes in Jing, Gongsun Zan blusters in You, Liu Yao clung to the Yangzi, and Liu Bei sparred along the Huai—so we never received orders to disarm.

sentences.zh: 今备、繇既破，操等饥馁，谓当与天下合谋，以诛丑类。

translations.literal: Now Bei and Yao are already broken, Cao and the others are hungry and exhausted; it is fitting that together with the realm we plot to execute the wicked sort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei and Liu Yao are broken; Cao Cao starves—this is the hour to join the world in cutting down the villains.

sentences.zh: 舍而不图，有自取之志，非海内所望，一也。

translations.literal: To set them aside and not plan against them, yet harbor ambition to seize power yourself, is not what the seas expect—that is the first count against the plan.
translations.idiomatic: First fault: you would ignore those rebels while grasping for the throne yourself—the realm will not call that righteous.

sentences.zh: 昔成汤伐桀，称有夏多罪；

translations.literal: In olden days Tang of Cheng attacked Jie of Xia, declaring that Xia had many crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Cheng attacked Jie because Xia was piled high with crimes;

sentences.zh: 武王伐纣，曰殷有罪罚重哉。

translations.literal: King Wu attacked Zhou of Shang, saying Yin had crimes and the punishment was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu marched on Zhou because Shang’s guilt was heavy and the sentence clear.

sentences.zh: 此二王者，虽有圣德，宜当君世；

translations.literal: These two kings, although they had sagely virtue, were fit to rule their age;
translations.idiomatic: Those two sages deserved the mandate,

sentences.zh: 如使不遭其时，亦无繇兴矣。

translations.literal: if they had not encountered their hour, neither would there have been cause to rise.
translations.idiomatic: yet neither would have struck had tyranny not given them the hour.

sentences.zh: 幼主非有恶於天下，徒以春秋尚少，胁於强臣，若无过而夺之，惧未合於汤、武之事，二也。

translations.literal: The young lord has no evil toward the realm; only because spring and autumn are still young he is coerced by strong ministers—if without fault you strip him, I fear it will not match the deeds of Tang and Wu—that is the second count.
translations.idiomatic: Second fault: the boy on the throne has not wronged the people—he is only young and bullied. To oust him without crime is no Tang–Wu revolution.

sentences.zh: 卓虽狂狡，至废主自与，亦犹未也，而天下闻其桀虐，攘臂同心而疾之，以中土希战之兵，当边地劲悍之虏，所以斯须游魂也。

translations.literal: Although Zhuo was wild and cunning, as for deposing the ruler and taking his place himself, he still had not reached that point, yet when the realm heard of his cruelty and tyranny, they rolled up sleeves with one heart and hated him; with troops of the central plains that seldom saw war, they faced the fierce barbarians of the borderlands—therefore in a moment he became a wandering ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo, for all his brutality, never dared take the throne himself; the empire rose as one and crushed him with militia that seldom saw battle—he became a flickering ghost overnight.

sentences.zh: 今四方之人，皆玩敌而便战斗矣，可得而胜者，以彼乱而我治，彼逆而我顺也。

translations.literal: Now the people of the four quarters all treat the enemy lightly and find battle convenient; what can be used to overcome them is that they are chaotic while we are ordered, they contrary while we compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Today every soldier knows how to fight; victory lies in our discipline against their chaos, our legitimacy against their rebellion.

sentences.zh: 见当世之纷若，欲大举以临之，適足趣祸，三也。

translations.literal: Seeing the confusion of the present age, if you wish greatly to raise forces against it, it only suffices to hasten disaster—that is the third count.
translations.idiomatic: Third fault: to launch a great war merely because the times look messy is to invite catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 天下神器，不可虚干，必须天赞与人力也。

translations.literal: The divine vessel of the realm cannot be grasped emptily; one must have Heaven’s aid together with human strength.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate cannot be seized in a void—it needs Heaven’s sign and human effort together.

sentences.zh: 殷汤有白鸠之祥，周武有赤乌之瑞，汉高有星聚之符，世祖有神光之徵，皆因民困悴於桀、纣之政，毒苦於秦、莽之役，故能芟去无道，致成其志。

translations.literal: Tang of Yin had the auspice of the white dove; King Wu of Zhou had the red crow; Han Gaozu had the omen of clustered stars; Shizu had the sign of divine light—they all took advantage of the people’s weariness and distress under the government of Jie and Zhou, their poison and bitterness under the labor of Qin and Mang, and therefore could mow down the wayless and accomplish their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Tang saw white birds, Wu a red crow, Gaozu a star-cluster, Guangwu a blaze of light—each struck when the people could no longer bear Jie, Zhou, Qin, or Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 今天下非患於幼主，未见受命之应验，而欲一旦卒然登即尊号，未之或有，四也。

translations.literal: Now the realm does not suffer from the young lord; one does not see responsive verification of receiving the mandate, yet you wish in one morning suddenly to ascend the honored title—never has such a thing existed—that is the fourth count.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth fault: the people do not blame the child emperor; no heaven-sent portent backs you; to leap to the throne overnight is without precedent.

sentences.zh: 天子之贵，四海之富，谁不欲焉？

translations.literal: The honor of the Son of Heaven, the wealth of the four seas—who does not desire them?
translations.idiomatic: Who would not want the throne and the wealth of the world?

sentences.zh: 义不可，势不得耳。

translations.literal: Righteousness does not permit it; circumstance does not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Duty forbids it, and the times will not bear it.

sentences.zh: 陈胜、项籍、王莽、公孙述之徒，皆南面称孤，莫之能济。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng, Xiang Ji, Wang Mang, Gongsun Shu and their sort all faced south calling themselves lords alone—none could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng, Xiang Yu, Wang Mang, Gongsun Shu—all crowned themselves and all fell.

sentences.zh: 帝王之位，不可横冀，五也。

translations.literal: The position of emperor-king cannot be rashly hoped for—that is the fifth count.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth fault: the dragon throne is not a prize for the reckless.

sentences.zh: 幼主岐嶷，若除其偪，去其鲠，必成中兴之业。

translations.literal: The young lord is precociously wise; if you remove what presses on him and extract what sticks in his throat, he is sure to complete the enterprise of mid-restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is bright; clear the thorns from his side and you midwife a true restoration.

sentences.zh: 夫致主於周成之盛，自受旦、奭之美，此诚所望於尊明也。

translations.literal: To bring the ruler to the splendor of King Cheng of Zhou, while yourself receiving the beauty of the Duke of Zhou and Shi—that is sincerely what is hoped from your enlightened honor.
translations.idiomatic: Guide him to the glory of King Cheng while you earn the name of the Duke of Zhou—that is what we beg of you.

sentences.zh: 纵使幼主有他改异，犹望推宗室之谱属，论近亲之贤良，以绍刘统，以固汉宗。

translations.literal: Even if the young lord should later change differently, still hope to push the genealogical ranks of the imperial house, discuss the worthy among close kin, thereby continuing the Liu line and consolidating the Han clan.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the boy emperor later falters, you can still seat another Liu of talent and keep the Han line alive.

sentences.zh: 皆所以书功金石，图形丹青，流庆无穷，垂声管纮。

translations.literal: All these are means by which merit is inscribed on metal and stone, forms are painted in cinnabar and blue, flowing blessing is without end, and sounds hang from pipes and strings.
translations.idiomatic: That path wins you bronze inscriptions, portrait galleries, endless blessing, and music in the temples.

sentences.zh: 舍而不为，为其难者，想明明之素，必所不忍，六也。

translations.literal: To set them aside and not do them, yet do what is difficult—I think your enlightened clarity in ordinary times surely cannot bear this—that is the sixth count.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth fault: to shun the hard right and choose the reckless wrong—your own clarity has never tolerated that.

sentences.zh: 五世为相，权之重，势之盛，天下莫得而比焉。

translations.literal: Five generations as chancellor—the weight of authority, the fullness of power—none under Heaven could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of your house held the chancellorship—no clan ever wielded such weight.

sentences.zh: 忠贞者必曰宜夙夜思惟，所以扶国家之踬顿，念社稷之危殆，以奉祖考之志，以报汉室之恩。

translations.literal: The loyal and true will surely say you ought day and night to ponder how to support the state’s stumbling, think on the altars’ peril, thereby to carry out the intent of the ancestors in the temple, thereby to repay the house of Han’s kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men will say you must shore up a tottering state, rescue the altars, honor your ancestors, and repay the Han.

sentences.zh: 其忽履道之节而强进取之欲者，将曰天下之人非家吏则门生也，孰不从我？

translations.literal: Those who neglect treading the way’s norms yet force the desire to seize advance will say, “The people of the realm are none other than household clerks or gate students—who will not follow me?
translations.idiomatic: The reckless will whisper, “Everyone is my client or pupil—who would refuse me?

sentences.zh: 四方之敌非吾匹则吾役也，谁能违我？

translations.literal: Enemies of the four quarters are none other than my mates or my servants—who can defy me?
translations.idiomatic: The world is either my peer or my serf—who can stand against me?

sentences.zh: 盍乘累世之势，起而取之哉？

translations.literal: Why not ride the momentum of many generations and rise to take it?”
translations.idiomatic: Why not use that piled-up power and seize the throne?”

sentences.zh: 二者殊数，不可不详察，七也。

translations.literal: The two sorts differ in reckoning; they cannot but be examined in detail—that is the seventh count.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh fault: those two voices are not the same—listen to which is Heaven and which is appetite.

sentences.zh: 所贵於圣哲者，以其审於机宜，慎於举措。

translations.literal: What is prized in sages and wise men is that they examine opportune timing and are cautious in initiating action.
translations.idiomatic: The wise judge the moment and move with care.

sentences.zh: 若难图之事，难保之势，以激群敌之气，以生众人之心，公义故不可，私计又不利，明哲不处，八也。

translations.literal: If in matters hard to plot and situations hard to preserve you arouse the qi of massed foes and give birth to the hearts of the multitude, public righteousness therefore cannot approve, private calculation again is not advantageous—the enlightened and wise do not dwell there—that is the eighth count.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth fault: a hopeless gamble that unites your enemies and breaks your own men serves neither honor nor interest.

sentences.zh: 世人多惑於图纬而牵非类，比合文字以悦所事，苟以阿上惑众，终有后悔者，自往迄今，未尝无之，不可不深择而熟思，九也。

translations.literal: Many in the age are deluded by charts and weft-texts and dragged by irrelevant comparisons, piecing together characters to please the business at hand; if for the sake of flattering superiors and deceiving the masses there will in the end be those who regret—from past to present it has never been otherwise—they cannot but choose deeply and think maturely—that is the ninth count.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth fault: apocryphal prophecies and forced word-play have ruined many who flattered a fad—study the past before you trust such glosses.

sentences.zh: 九者，尊明所见之餘耳，庶备起予，补所遗忘。

translations.literal: The nine counts are what remains beyond your enlightened view; perhaps they may supply what rouses me and repair what was forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: These nine points are only what your own light may have missed—take them as footnotes to your conscience.

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，幸留神听！

translations.literal: Loyal words offend the ear; I hope you will keep spirit and listen!
translations.idiomatic: Truth grates on the ear—yet please hear us out.

sentences.zh: 」《典略》云张昭之辞。

translations.literal: The Dianlüe states they were Zhang Zhao’s words.
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe attributes the letter to Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为张昭虽名重，然不如纮之文也，此书必纮所作。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks that although Zhang Zhao’s name was weighty, he was not equal to Hong’s literary skill; this letter must be Hong’s composition.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argues that Zhang Zhao, famous as he was, could not match Zhang Hong’s prose—this piece must be Hong’s work.〉

sentences.zh: 後術死，長史楊弘、大將張勳等將其眾欲就策，廬江太守劉勳要擊，悉虜之，收其珍寶以歸。

translations.literal: Later when Shu died, Chief Clerk Yang Hong, great general Zhang Xun, and others led his masses wishing to join Ce; Grand Administrator of Lujiang Liu Xun ambushed and struck them, all captured them, and seized their precious treasures and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shu died, Yang Hong and Zhang Xun tried to lead his host to Sun Ce, but Liu Xun of Lujiang ambushed them, took all, and pocketed the loot.

sentences.zh: 策聞之，偽與勳好盟。

translations.literal: When Ce heard it, he feigned friendship and alliance with Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce pretended friendship with Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳新得術眾，時豫章上繚宗民萬餘家在江東。

translations.literal: Xun had newly obtained Shu’s masses; at that time in Yuzhang at Shangliao more than ten thousand households of lineage people were east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun had just absorbed Yuan Shu’s army, while ten thousand clan households of Shangliao in Yuzhang still camped east of the river.

sentences.zh: 策勸勳攻取之。

translations.literal: Ce urged Xun to attack and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce urged him to conquer Shangliao.

sentences.zh: 勳既行，策輕軍晨夜襲拔廬江，勳眾盡降，勳獨與麾下數百人自歸曹公。

translations.literal: After Xun had marched, Ce with light troops by day and night suddenly attacked and took Lujiang; Xun’s masses all surrendered; Xun alone with several hundred followers under his command himself returned to Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xun marched off, Sun Ce stormed Lujiang by night, accepted his army’s surrender, and drove Liu Xun himself to Cao Cao with a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策被诏敕，与司空曹公、卫将军董承、益州牧刘璋等并力讨袁术、刘表。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Ce received an edict ordering him, together with Minister of Works Lord Cao, Guard General Dong Cheng, Shepherd of Yizhou Liu Zhang, and others, to join strength in punishing Yuan Shu and Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says an edict bound Sun Ce with Cao Cao, Dong Cheng, and Liu Zhang in a league against Yuan Shu and Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 军严当进，会术死，术从弟胤、女婿黄猗等畏惧曹公，不敢守寿春，乃共舁术棺柩，扶其妻子及部曲男女，就刘勋於皖城。

translations.literal: The army was strict and about to advance when it happened that Shu died; Shu’s cousin Yin, son-in-law Huang Yi, and others feared Lord Cao and did not dare defend Shouchun; they together carried Shu’s coffin, supported his wife and children and male and female retainers, and went to Liu Xun at Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The host was ready to march when Yuan Shu died; Yuan Yin, Huang Yi, and the rest, dreading Cao Cao, abandoned Shouchun, bore Yuan Shu’s coffin, and shepherded family and troops to Liu Xun at Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 勋粮食少，无以相振，乃遣从弟偕告籴於豫章太守华歆。

translations.literal: Xun had little grain and nothing with which mutually to aid; thereupon he sent his cousin Xie to beg grain from Grand Administrator of Yuzhang Hua Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun ran short of food and sent his cousin to borrow grain from Hua Xin in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歆郡素少谷，遣吏将偕就海昏上缭，使诸宗帅共出三万斛米以与偕。

translations.literal: Xin’s commandery always had little grain; he sent an officer to lead Xie to Haihun Shangliao, making the various lineage chiefs together issue thirty thousand hu of rice to give to Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin’s granaries were thin; he sent an escort to Shangliao near Haihun and squeezed thirty thousand hu from the clan headmen for Liu Xun’s envoy.

sentences.zh: 偕往历月，才得数千斛。

translations.literal: Xie went for passing months and only obtained several thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy lingered a month and brought back only a few thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 偕乃报勋，具说形状，使勋来袭取之。

translations.literal: Xie thereupon reported to Xun, fully stating the shape of affairs, making Xun come strike and take them.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Liu Xun that rich stores lay at Shangliao and baited him to march.

sentences.zh: 勋得偕书，使潜军到海昏邑下。

translations.literal: Xun obtained Xie’s letter and sent a concealed army to the foot of Haihun county.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun read the letter and slipped a column toward Haihun.

sentences.zh: 宗帅知之，空壁逃匿，勋了无所得。

translations.literal: The lineage chiefs knew it, emptied the walls and fled and hid; Xun completely obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The headmen emptied their forts and vanished; Liu Xun seized nothing.

sentences.zh: 时策西讨黄祖，行及石城，闻勋轻身诣海昏，便分遣从兄贲、辅率八千人於彭泽待勋，自与周瑜率二万人步袭皖城，即克之，得术百工及鼓吹部曲三万餘人，并术、勋妻子。

translations.literal: At that time Ce was campaigning west against Huang Zu; proceeding as far as Shicheng, he heard Xun had gone in person to Haihun; thereupon he separately dispatched his cousin Ben and Fu leading eight thousand men to await Xun at Pengze; he himself with Zhou Yu led twenty thousand men on foot to raid Wancheng, immediately took it, obtained Shu’s hundred craftsmen and military bands and retainers more than thirty thousand men, together with Shu’s and Xun’s wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was already marching against Huang Zu; at Shicheng he learned Liu Xun had gone to Shangliao. He sent Sun Ben and Sun Fu with eight thousand men to block Pengze, then took twenty thousand foot with Zhou Yu, stormed Wancheng, captured Yuan Shu’s artisans, musicians, and thirty thousand troops, together with both families.

sentences.zh: 表用汝南李术为庐江太守，给兵三千人以守皖，皆徙所得人东诣吴。

translations.literal: Biao employed Li Shu of Runan as Grand Administrator of Lujiang, giving three thousand troops to guard Wancheng; all moved the people obtained east to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao named Li Shu prefect of Lujiang with three thousand guards, while Sun Ce marched the captives east to Wu.

sentences.zh: 贲、辅又於彭泽破勋。

translations.literal: Ben and Fu again at Pengze defeated Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ben and Sun Fu smashed Liu Xun again at Pengze.

sentences.zh: 勋走入楚江，从寻阳步上到置马亭，闻策等已克皖，乃投西塞。

translations.literal: Xun fled into the Chu River, from Xunyang on foot ascended to the horse-posting station, heard Ce and the others had already taken Wancheng, thereupon threw himself to Xisai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun fled up the Chu water, trudged from Xunyang toward the courier station, learned Wancheng had fallen, and bolted for Xisai.

sentences.zh: 至沂，筑垒自守，告急於刘表，求救於黄祖。

translations.literal: Reaching Yi, he piled ramparts to defend himself, urgently reported to Liu Biao, and begged rescue from Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: At Yi he threw up walls, begged Liu Biao for help, and called on Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 祖遣太子射船军五千人助勋。

translations.literal: Zu dispatched five thousand boat-borne archers to aid Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu sent five thousand marine archers in war boats to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 策复就攻，大破勋。

translations.literal: Ce again went and attacked, greatly defeated Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce struck again and shattered Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 勋与偕北归曹公，射亦遁走。

translations.literal: Xun with Xie northward returned to Lord Cao; the archers also fled and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun and his cousin fled north to Cao Cao, and Huang Zu’s bowmen scattered as well.

sentences.zh: 策收得勋兵二千餘人，船千艘，遂前进夏口攻黄祖。

translations.literal: Ce collected and obtained more than two thousand of Xun’s soldiers, a thousand boats, and thereupon advanced to Xiakou to attack Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce picked up two thousand prisoners, a thousand hulls, and swept on to Xiakou against Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 时刘表遣从子虎、南阳韩晞将长矛五千，来为黄祖前锋。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Biao dispatched his nephew Hu and Han Xi of Nanyang leading five thousand long-spearmen, coming to be Huang Zu’s van.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent his nephew Liu Hu and Han Xi of Nanyang with five thousand pikemen to spearhead Huang Zu’s line.

sentences.zh: 策与战，大破之。

translations.literal: Ce joined battle with them and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce met them in battle and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 吴录载策表曰：「臣讨黄祖，以十二月八日到祖所屯沙羡县。

translations.literal: The Wu Lu records Ce’s memorial, saying, “Your subject campaigned against Huang Zu and on the eighth day of the twelfth month reached the place where Zu was encamped at Shaxian in Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Lu quotes Sun Ce’s memorial: “On the eighth of the twelfth month I reached Huang Zu’s camp at Shaxian in Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 刘表遣将助祖，并来趣臣。

translations.literal: Liu Biao dispatched generals to aid Zu, and together they came to press your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent reinforcements to hurry against me.

sentences.zh: 臣以十一日平旦部所领江夏太守行建威中郎将周瑜、领桂阳太守行征虏中郎将吕范、领零陵太守行荡寇中郎将程普、行奉业校尉孙权、行先登校尉韩当、行武锋校尉黄盖等同时俱进。

translations.literal: Your subject on the eleventh day at dawn arrayed those led—acting Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and acting Colonel Who Establishes Might Zhou Yu, acting Grand Administrator of Guilin and acting Colonel Who Captures Caitiffs Lü Fan, acting Grand Administrator of Lingling and acting Colonel Who Sweeps Caitiffs Cheng Pu, acting Colonel Who Upholds Enterprise Sun Quan, acting Colonel Who Leads the Vanguard Han Dang, acting Colonel Who Rakes the Van Huang Gai—and others, all advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on the eleventh I sent Zhou Yu, Lü Fan, Cheng Pu, Sun Quan, Han Dang, and Huang Gai—each in his acting river command and colonel’s rank—forward in one line.

sentences.zh: 身跨马栎陈，手击急鼓，以齐战势。

translations.literal: Your subject personally mounted a horse, spread the lines, hand struck the urgent drum to align the battle momentum.
translations.idiomatic: I myself rode the line, beat the war drum, and set the tempo of the assault.

sentences.zh: 吏士奋激，踊跃百倍，心精意果，各竞用命。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were roused and excited, leaping and bounding a hundredfold; hearts were keen and wills firm, each competing to expend life.
translations.idiomatic: The men surged forward with redoubled fury, each striving to spend his life well.

sentences.zh: 越渡重堑，迅疾若飞。

translations.literal: They crossed layered moats, swift and fast as if flying.
translations.idiomatic: They vaulted the trenches like birds in flight.

sentences.zh: 火放上风，兵激烟下，弓弩并发，流矢雨集，日加辰时，祖乃溃烂。

translations.literal: Fire was set upwind, soldiers dashed below the smoke, crossbows loosed together, streaming arrows gathered like rain; by the chen hour of daylight Zu thereupon was routed.
translations.idiomatic: We fired upwind, charged under the smoke, and poured volleys until, past mid-morning, Huang Zu’s line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 锋刃所截，猋火所焚，前无生寇，惟祖迸走。

translations.literal: Where sharp blades cut, where leaping fire burned, ahead there were no living bandits; only Zu broke line and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Blade and flame left no standing foe—only Huang Zu broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 获其妻息男女七人，斩虎、

translations.literal: They captured his wife and children, seven persons male and female, beheaded Hu,
translations.idiomatic: We took his household, seven souls, struck down Liu Hu,

translations.literal: (marginal variant reads “wolf”)
translations.idiomatic: (Manuscript variant for the preceding name.)

sentences.zh: 韩晞已下二万餘级，其赴水溺者一万餘口，船六千餘艘，财物山积。

translations.literal: From Han Xi downward more than twenty thousand heads were taken; those who rushed into the water and drowned numbered more than ten thousand persons; boats were more than six thousand; goods and wealth piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: We struck down Han Xi and more than twenty thousand besides; over ten thousand drowned trying to escape; we seized six thousand boats and mountains of plunder.

sentences.zh: 虽表未禽，祖宿狡猾，为表腹心，出作爪牙，表之鸱张，以祖气息，而祖家属部曲，扫地无餘，表孤特之虏，成鬼行尸。

translations.literal: Although Biao was not yet captured, Zu long was crafty, was Biao’s belly and heart, went out as claws and fangs; Biao’s arrogance depended on Zu’s breath; yet Zu’s family members and retainers were swept to the ground without remainder—Biao is an isolated captive, a demon walking in a corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao himself escaped, but Huang Zu was his claws; with Zu’s clan wiped out, Liu Biao is a headless shell, a corpse still walking.

sentences.zh: 诚皆圣朝神武远振，臣讨有罪，得效微勤。」〉

translations.literal: Truly all is the sage court’s divine martialness extending far; your subject punished the guilty and was able to render slight service.”〉
translations.idiomatic: All this is Your Majesty’s distant awe; I only did my small part against a criminal.”〉

sentences.zh: 是時袁紹方強，而策並江東，曹公力未能逞，且欲撫之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shao was just strong, while Ce annexed Jiangdong; Lord Cao’s strength was not yet able to assert itself, and moreover he wished to soothe him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao still dominated the north while Sun Ce held the east; Cao Cao could not yet strike east and chose to conciliate him.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：曹公闻策平定江南，意甚难之，常呼「猘兒难与争锋也」。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Li states: When Lord Cao heard Ce had pacified south of the Yangzi, his mind was greatly troubled; he often called out, “That whelp is hard to match point to point.”〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Li says Cao Cao groaned that Sun Ce had pacified the south—“that pup is a foe you cannot meet head-on.”〉

sentences.zh: 乃以弟女配策小弟匡，又為子彰取賁女，皆禮辟策弟權、翊，又命揚州刺史嚴象舉權茂才。

translations.literal: Thereupon he matched his younger brother’s daughter to Ce’s younger brother Kuang, and again for his son Zhang took Ben’s daughter, all with ceremonial summons to Ce’s younger brothers Quan and Yi, and again ordered Inspector of Yangzhou Yan Xiang to recommend Quan as maocai.
translations.idiomatic: He married a niece to Sun Kuang, wed Cao Zhang to Sun Ben’s daughter, summoned Sun Quan and Sun Yi with court ceremony, and had Yan Xiang nominate Sun Quan as maocai.

sentences.zh: 先是，策殺貢，貢小子與客亡匿江邊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ce had killed Gong; Gong’s young son with retainers fled and hid along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Ce had executed Xu Gong; the prefect’s young son and his clients hid along the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 策單騎出，卒與客遇，客擊傷策。

translations.literal: Ce rode out alone on one horse, suddenly met the retainers, and the retainers struck and wounded Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce rode out alone, blundered into them, and they wounded him.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：广陵太守陈登治射阳，登即瑀之从兄子也。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Grand Administrator of Guangling Chen Deng administered Sheyang; Deng was the son of Chen Yu’s elder brother’s son.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan names Guangling’s prefect Chen Deng—nephew of Chen Yu—who ruled from Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 策前西征，登阴复遣间使，以印绶与严白虎餘党，图为后害，以报瑀见破之辱。

translations.literal: Before Ce’s western campaign, Deng secretly again dispatched secret agents, with seals and ribbons to Yan Baihu’s remaining faction, plotting to be a later harm, to repay the shame of Yu being broken.
translations.idiomatic: Before Sun Ce marched west, Chen Deng secretly armed the remnants of Yan Baihu, hoping to stab him in the back for the ruin of Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 策归，复讨登。

translations.literal: When Ce returned, again he campaigned against Deng.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Sun Ce turned against Chen Deng.

sentences.zh: 军到丹徒，须待运粮。

translations.literal: The army reached Dantu, waiting for transport of grain.
translations.idiomatic: His army halted at Dantu waiting for grain boats.

sentences.zh: 策性好猎，将步骑数出。

translations.literal: Ce by nature loved hunting, leading infantry and cavalry out several times.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce loved the chase and often rode out with a mixed escort.

sentences.zh: 策驱驰逐鹿，所乘马精骏，从骑绝不能及。

translations.literal: Ce galloped chasing deer; the horse he rode was refined and swift, and following cavalry absolutely could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred a superb mount after deer and outdistanced every follower.

sentences.zh: 初，吴郡太守许贡上表於汉帝曰：「孙策骁雄，与项籍相似，宜加贵宠，召还京邑。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery Xu Gong upward memorialized to the Han emperor, saying, “Sun Ce is a fierce champion, similar to Xiang Ji; it is fitting to add noble favor and summon him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu’s prefect Xu Gong memorialized the throne: “Sun Ce is another Xiang Yu—honor him and recall him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 若被诏不得不还，若放於外必作世患。

translations.literal: If he receives the edict he cannot but return; if he is released outside he is sure to become a generation’s calamity.”
translations.idiomatic: If summoned he must obey; if left abroad he will plague the age.”

sentences.zh: 」策候吏得贡表，以示策。

translations.literal: Ce’s watch officer obtained Gong’s memorial and showed it to Ce.
translations.idiomatic: A patrol seized Xu Gong’s memorial and handed it to Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策请贡相见，以责让贡。

translations.literal: Ce requested Gong to meet face to face, thereby blaming Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce called Xu Gong in and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 贡辞无表，策即令武士绞杀之。

translations.literal: Gong’s words denied there was a memorial; Ce immediately ordered martial gentlemen to strangle and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gong denied writing it; Sun Ce had him strangled on the spot.

sentences.zh: 贡奴客潜民间，欲为贡报雠。

translations.literal: Gong’s slaves and retainers hid among the common people, wishing to avenge Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gong’s household hid in the countryside, plotting revenge for their master.

sentences.zh: 猎日，卒有三人即贡客也。

translations.literal: On a hunting day, finally there were three men who were Gong’s retainers.
translations.idiomatic: One day on the hunt three of Xu Gong’s men turned up in his path.

sentences.zh: 策问：「尔等何人？

translations.literal: Ce asked, “Who are you people?”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce demanded, “Who are you?”

sentences.zh: 」答云：「是韩当兵，在此射鹿耳。

translations.literal: They answered, saying, “We are Han Dang’s soldiers, here shooting deer.”
translations.idiomatic: They lied, “We’re men of Han Dang’s command, out after deer.”

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「当兵吾皆识之，未尝见汝等。

translations.literal: Ce said, “As for soldiers, I all know them; I have never seen you lot.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, “I know every man in Han Dang’s unit—I’ve never seen you.”

sentences.zh: 」因射一人，应弦而倒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he shot one man; with the twang of the string he fell.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed an arrow and dropped one where he stood.

sentences.zh: 餘二人怖急，便举弓射策，中颊。

translations.literal: The remaining two men were frightened and pressed; thereupon they raised bows and shot Ce, hitting his cheek.
translations.idiomatic: The other two panicked, shot back, and tore his cheek open.

sentences.zh: 后骑寻至，皆刺杀之。

translations.literal: Rear riders soon arrived and all stabbed them to death.
translations.idiomatic: His escort galloped up and speared them dead.

sentences.zh: 《九州春秋》曰：策闻曹公北征柳城，悉起江南之众，自号大司马，将北袭许，恃其勇，行不设备，故及於难。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou Chunqiu states: Ce heard Lord Cao was campaigning north to Liucheng, fully raised the masses south of the Yangzi, styled himself Grand Marshal, intended to raid Xu northward, relied on his courage, went without setting precautions, therefore met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou Chunqiu claims Sun Ce heard Cao Cao had gone north against Liucheng, called out every southern soldier, named himself grand marshal, and meant to strike the capital—overconfident and unguarded, he courted death.

sentences.zh: 孙盛《异同评》曰：凡此数书，各有所失。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng’s Yitong Ping states: Generally these several documents each have what they miss.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng’s comparative review says each of those sources errs in its own way.

sentences.zh: 孙策虽威行江外，略有六郡，然黄祖乘其上流，陈登间其心腹，且深险强宗，未尽归复，曹、袁虎争，势倾山海，策岂暇远师汝、颍，而迁帝於吴、越哉？

translations.literal: Although Sun Ce’s awesomeness extended beyond the Yangzi and he roughly held six commanderies, yet Huang Zu rode his upper stream, Chen Deng sundered his belly and heart, and moreover deep-gorge strong lineages had not all returned in submission; Cao and Yuan were tigers contending, momentum overturned mountain and sea—how could Ce have leisure for distant campaigns to Ru and Ying and for moving the emperor to Wu and Yue?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce’s fame ran south of the river and he held six commanderies, yet Huang Zu still straddled the upper Jing, Chen Deng gnawed at his flank, and powerful clans in the hills had not all yielded; Cao Cao and Yuan Shao were tearing the north apart—could he spare troops for a march on Run–Ying or for dragging the emperor down to Wu–Yue?

sentences.zh: 斯盖庸人之所鉴见，况策达於事势者乎？

translations.literal: This is what mediocre men can see in a mirror—how much more Ce, who understood affairs’ momentum?
translations.idiomatic: Any dullard could see that—let alone Sun Ce, who read the strategic map.

sentences.zh: 又案袁绍以建安五年至黎阳，而策以四月遇害，而志云策闻曹公与绍相拒於官渡，谬矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining the fact that Yuan Shao in the fifth year of Jian’an reached Liyang, while Ce was killed in the fourth month, yet the zhi says Ce heard Lord Cao and Shao resisting each other at Guandu—wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao did not reach Liyang until Jian’an 5, while Sun Ce died in the fourth month of that year; to say he heard of Guandu is simply wrong.

sentences.zh: 伐登之言，为有证也。

translations.literal: The words about attacking Deng have evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The story that he was marching against Chen Deng rests on firmer ground.

sentences.zh: 又江表传说策悉识韩当军士，疑此为诈，便射杀一人。

translations.literal: Again the Jiang Biao Zhuan says Ce entirely knew Han Dang’s soldiers, doubted this was deception, then shot and killed one man.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang Biao Zhuan adds that Sun Ce knew every face in Han Dang’s ranks, saw through the impostors, and shot one—

sentences.zh: 夫三军将士或有新附，策为大将，何能悉识？

translations.literal: As for the three armies’ soldiers and generals, some have newly submitted; Ce as great general—how could he entirely know them?
translations.idiomatic: —yet hosts always include new recruits; no commander knows every private by sight.

sentences.zh: 以所不识，便射杀之，非其论也，又策见杀在五年，柳城之役在十二年，《九州春秋》乖错尤甚矣。

translations.literal: Because of not recognizing them then to shoot and kill them is not that theory; moreover Ce was killed in the fifth year, the Liucheng campaign was in the twelfth year—the Jiuzhou Chunqiu’s contradictions are especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: To kill strangers on suspicion is another matter; Sun Ce died in 200, Cao’s Liucheng campaign was in 207—the Jiuzhou Chunqiu is wildly off.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：《傅子》亦云曹公征柳城，将袭许。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: The Fuzi likewise says Lord Cao campaigned to Liucheng, intending to raid Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that the Fuzi repeats the tale of a northern raid on the capital from Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 记述若斯，何其疏哉！

translations.literal: Records and narratives like this—how careless!
translations.idiomatic: When memorials contradict dates this badly, the editing was slipshod.

sentences.zh: 然孙盛所讥，未为悉是。

translations.literal: Yet Sun Sheng’s ridicule is not entirely correct.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Sun Sheng’s dismissal goes too far.

sentences.zh: 黄祖始被策破，魂气未反，

translations.literal: Huang Zu at first was broken by Ce; soul and breath had not yet returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu had just been shattered by Sun Ce and was still reeling.

translations.literal: (Marginal gloss: the character dan, “only.”)
translations.idiomatic: (Manuscript gloss: “only.”)

sentences.zh: 刘表君臣本无兼并之志，虽在上流，何办规拟吴会？

translations.literal: Liu Biao’s ruler and ministers from the beginning lacked ambition to annex; although on the upper stream, how could they manage to plan against Wu and Hui?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao’s court never dreamed of swallowing the southeast; holding the upper river did not mean they could strike at Wu.

sentences.zh: 策之此举，理应先图陈登，但举兵所在，不止登而已。

translations.literal: As for this move of Ce, by principle he ought first to plan against Chen Deng, but the places where he raised troops were not only Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce’s next move should have been Chen Deng, but his columns had more than one target.

sentences.zh: 于时强宗骁帅，祖郎、严虎之徒，禽灭已尽，所餘山越，盖何足虑？

translations.literal: At that time strong-lineage fierce commanders like Zu Lang, Yan Hu, and their sort, capture and extinction were already complete; what remained of the mountain Yue—how could they be worth concern?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Lang, Yan Hu, and the other band chiefs were already gone; the scattered Yue hillmen hardly threatened a great army.

sentences.zh: 然则策之所规，未可谓之不暇也。

translations.literal: Then Ce’s plans cannot be said to lack leisure.
translations.idiomatic: So Sun Ce was not without time for further design.

sentences.zh: 若使策志获从，大权在手，淮、泗之间，所在皆可都，何必毕志江外，其当迁帝於扬、越哉？

translations.literal: If Ce’s intentions had been followed, great authority in hand, between Huai and Si wherever could all be made a capital—why must he exhaust his purpose outside the Yangzi—would he necessarily move the emperor to Yang and Yue?
translations.idiomatic: Had his luck held and power stayed in his hands, the Huai–Si plain offered many sites for a capital; he need not have chained himself to the lower Yangzi or dreamed of hauling the court to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 案

translations.literal: According to
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cites

sentences.zh: 〈魏武纪〉

translations.literal: the “Annals of Emperor Wu of Wei”
translations.idiomatic: the Wei Annals’ “Basic Annals of Emperor Wu”

sentences.zh: ，武帝以建安四年已出屯官渡，乃策未死之前，久与袁绍交兵，则《国志》所云不为谬也。

translations.literal: , Emperor Wu in the fourth year of Jian’an already went out to encamp at Guandu—this was before Ce’s death—long exchanging troops with Yuan Shao; therefore what the Guo zhi says is not erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: shows Cao Cao already camped at Guandu in Jian’an 4, before Sun Ce died, locked with Yuan Shao for months—so the Guo zhi is not mistaken on timing.

sentences.zh: 许贡客。

translations.literal: Xu Gong’s retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The clients of Xu Gong.

sentences.zh: 无闻之小人，而能感识恩遇，临义忘生，卒然奋发，有侔古烈矣。

translations.literal: Unknown petty men, yet able to feel and know received kindness, facing righteousness forgot life, suddenly roused to action, comparable to ancient fierce integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Obscure men who repaid a patron’s kindness with their lives, rising like heroes of old.

sentences.zh: 诗云：「君子有徽猷，小人与属。

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says, “The gentleman has fine plans; the petty man attaches to them.”
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, “The nobleman lays wise plans, and lesser men cleave to them.”

sentences.zh: 」贡客其有焉。〉

translations.literal: Gong’s retainers may have had that.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gong’s men lived up to that verse.〉

sentences.zh: 創甚，請張昭等謂曰：「中國方亂，夫以吳、越之眾，三江之固，足以觀成敗。

translations.literal: The wound was severe; he requested Zhang Zhao and others, saying to them, “The central states are just in chaos; with Wu and Yue’s masses and the three rivers’ solidity, it suffices to watch success or failure.”
translations.idiomatic: His wounds were grave; he called Zhang Zhao and the rest and said, “The heartland is in turmoil; with our hosts south of the Yangzi and the barrier of the three rivers we can wait out the storm.”

sentences.zh: 公等善相吾弟！

translations.literal: Gentlemen, tend well to my younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen, serve my brother well.

sentences.zh: 」呼權佩以印綬，謂曰：「舉江東之眾，決機於兩陳

translations.literal: He called Quan, hung seals and ribbons on him, saying, “Raise the masses east of the Yangzi, decide the moment between two formations
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Sun Quan, hung the seal and ribbon on him, and said, “To marshal the armies east of the river and settle the issue between two battle lines

translations.literal: (textual variant: the character zhen, “battle formation.”)
translations.idiomatic: (Manuscript variant reads zhen, “formation.”)

sentences.zh: 之間，與天下爭衡，卿不如我。

translations.literal: among them, and contend for balance with the realm—you are not my match.”
translations.idiomatic: and wrest the empire for advantage—you are not my equal.”

sentences.zh: 舉賢任能，各盡其心，以保江東，我不如卿。

translations.literal: “Raise the worthy and employ the capable, each exhausting his heart, to protect east of the Yangzi—I am not your match.”
translations.idiomatic: “To raise able men and let each give his utmost in guarding the southeast—that is where I fall short of you.”

sentences.zh: 」至夜卒，時年二十六。

translations.literal: He died before night; at that time his age was twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died that night at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：策既被创，医言可治，当好自将护，百日勿动。

translations.literal: The Wu Li states: After Ce was wounded, the doctors said it could be cured, that he ought well to guard himself, and for a hundred days not move.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Li says the physicians promised a cure if he rested quietly for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 策引镜自照，谓左右曰：「面如此，尚可复建功立事乎？

translations.literal: Ce drew a mirror to look at himself, said to those at his side, “With a face like this, can I still again establish merit and affairs?”
translations.idiomatic: He lifted a mirror and asked his attendants, “Could a face like this ever lead armies again?”

sentences.zh: 」椎几大奋，创皆分裂，其夜卒。

translations.literal: He pounded the table greatly in rage; the wounds all split apart; that night he died.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed the table in fury; his wounds tore open, and he died before morning.

sentences.zh: 《搜神记》曰：策既杀于吉，每独坐，彷彿见吉在左右，意深恶之，颇有失常。

translations.literal: The Soushen Ji states: After Ce had killed Yu Ji, whenever sitting alone, dimly as if he saw Ji at left and right, his mind deeply hated it and somewhat lost normal composure.
translations.idiomatic: The Soushen Ji claims that after executing the Daoist Yu Ji he thought he saw the ghost at his elbow and grew unhinged.

sentences.zh: 后治创方差，而引镜自照，见吉在镜中，顾而弗见，如是再三，因扑镜大叫，创皆崩裂，须臾而死。〉

translations.literal: Later, when treating the wounds had just improved, yet drawing the mirror to look at himself, he saw Ji in the mirror; he looked around but did not see him; like this again three times; therefore he threw the mirror and shouted greatly; the wounds all burst open; in a moment he died.〉
translations.idiomatic: When the wounds had begun to heal he looked again and saw Yu Ji in the glass—turned his head and saw nothing—three times over, until he dashed the mirror and screamed; the cuts burst and he was dead in moments.〉

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，追謚策曰長沙桓王，封子紹為吳侯，後改封上虞侯。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the honored title, he posthumously titled Ce Prince Huan of Changsha, enfeoffed son Shao as Marquis of Wu, later changed the enfeoffment to Marquis of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan took the throne he canonized Sun Ce as Prince Huan of Changsha, made Sun Shao marquis of Wu, later shifted the fief to Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 紹卒，子奉嗣。

translations.literal: Shao died; son Feng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao died and his son Sun Feng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，訛言謂奉當立，誅死。

translations.literal: In Sun Hao’s time, a false rumor said Feng would be established; he was executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao a rumor named Sun Feng as the true heir; the court put him to death.

sentences.zh: 作者評論

translations.literal: Author commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary by the compiler.

sentences.zh: 評曰：「孫堅勇摯剛毅，孤微發跡，導溫戮卓，山陵杜塞，有忠壯之烈。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: “Sun Jian was brave, ardent, firm, and stern; from humble isolation he rose to eminence, guided Wen and slew Zhuo, blocked imperial tombs with earth—he had fierce loyalty and stalwart heroism.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict runs: “Sun Jian was bold and iron-willed, a man of no pedigree who still defied Zhang Wen, cut down Dong Zhuo, and refilled the looted tombs—a loyal champion.

sentences.zh: 策英氣傑濟，猛銳冠世，覽奇取異，志陵中夏。

translations.literal: Ce’s heroic qi was outstanding and vast, fierce and sharp surpassing the age, gathered strange and took the unusual—his ambition towered over central Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce blazed with genius, outfought every rival of his day, and aimed his spear at the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 然皆輕佻果躁，隕身致敗。

translations.literal: Yet both were frivolous, reckless, and hasty, cast away their persons and brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both were rash and headstrong, and their impatience cost them their lives.

sentences.zh: 且割據江東，策之基兆也。

translations.literal: Moreover cutting off and occupying east of the Yangzi was Ce’s founding augury.
translations.idiomatic: The carve-up of the southeast was Sun Ce’s founding stroke.

sentences.zh: 而權尊祟未至，子止侯爵，於義儉矣。」

translations.literal: Yet Quan’s honoring respect had not yet reached the top; the son stopped at marquis rank—by righteousness it was stingy.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan’s later honors stopped short of an imperial shrine for his brother, and the heir held only a marquisate—mean by any standard of right.”

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：孫氏兄弟皆明略絕群。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: The Sun brothers each had clear strategy surpassing the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng adds that both brothers were strategists without peer.

sentences.zh: 創基立事，策之由也，自臨終之日，顧命委權。

translations.literal: Establishing foundation and establishing affairs came from Ce; from the day of facing death he entrusted Quan with the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce laid the state’s foundations; with his dying breath he handed the seal to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 夫意氣之間，猶有刎頸，況天倫之篤愛，豪達之英鑑，豈吝名號於既往，違本情之至實哉？

translations.literal: Between temper and qi there is yet neck-cutting friendship—how much more Heaven-patterned deep love and heroic insight—would he be stingy with names and titles toward what is past, violating utmost truth of original feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Friends swear to die for each other—would brothers bound by blood stint on a posthumous throne-name and betray their own hearts?

sentences.zh: 抑將遠思虛盈之數，而慎其名器者乎？

translations.literal: Or perhaps it was thinking far on void and full’s numbers, and being careful with names and regalia?
translations.idiomatic: Or did he weigh the balance of power and guard the symbols of rule?

sentences.zh: 夫正本定名，為國之大防；

translations.literal: Correcting root and fixing name is the state’s great dike;
translations.idiomatic: Setting the right heir and the right title is the dyke that holds a realm;

sentences.zh: 杜絕疑貳，消釁之良謨。

translations.literal: Cutting off doubt and twoness is the good plan to dissolve strife.
translations.idiomatic: cutting off rival claimants is the surest way to smother civil war.

sentences.zh: 是故魯隱矜義，終致羽父之禍；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Yin of Lu prized small righteousness and in the end brought Duke Yufu’s disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yin of Lu clung to petty honor and brought down Yufu’s revolt;

sentences.zh: 宋宣懷仁，卒有殤公之哀。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan of Song cherished benevolence and in the end had the grief of Duke Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuan of Song’s soft heart ended in the tragedy of Duke Shang.

sentences.zh: 皆心存小善，而不達經綸之圖；

translations.literal: All stored small goodness in the heart but did not comprehend the diagrams of ordering the warp;
translations.idiomatic: They cherished small kindness and missed the larger design;

sentences.zh: 求譽當年，而不思貽厥之謀。

translations.literal: Sought praise in that year but did not think of bequeathing heirs’ plots.
translations.idiomatic: they chased the praise of the moment and forgot the succession.

sentences.zh: 可謂輕千乘之國，蹈道則未也。

translations.literal: One may call it treating lightly a state of a thousand chariots—as for treading the way, it had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They gambled a great state on sentiment and never reached the true path.

sentences.zh: 孫氏因擾攘之際，得奮其縱橫之志，業非積德之基，邦無磐石之固，勢一則祿祚可終，情乖則禍亂塵起，安可不防微於未兆，慮難於將來？

translations.literal: The Sun clan took advantage of turmoil’s moment, could exert their crisscrossing ambition; their enterprise was not a foundation of accumulated virtue, their state lacked solidity like rock—when momentum unified then salary and blessing could end, when affections diverged then calamity and chaos arose in dust—how could one not guard against the subtle before omens appear, think on difficulty in the future?
translations.idiomatic: The Suns seized a moment of chaos; their power rested on the sword, not on long virtue, and their realm lacked bedrock—unity bought peace, a rift brought storm—so the wise watch the first spark and plan before the flood.

sentences.zh: 壯哉！

translations.literal: How stalwart!
translations.idiomatic: How magnificent a beginning!

sentences.zh: 策為首事之君，有吳開國之主；

translations.literal: Ce was the lord who first raised the affair, Wu’s lord who opened the state;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was the founder in the field, the true begetter of Wu;

sentences.zh: 將相在列，皆其舊也，而嗣子弱劣，析薪弗荷，奉援則魯桓、田巿之難作，崇之則與夷、子馮之禍興。

translations.literal: generals and ministers in the ranks were all his old followers, yet the heir son was weak and inferior, could not shoulder splitting firewood—if one supported according to precedent then the difficulties of Duke Huan of Lu and Tian Shi arise, if one exalted then the disasters of Yu Yi and Zi Feng arise.
translations.idiomatic: yet his generals were his veterans while the boy heir was frail—support him and you risk Lu Huan’s coup, exalt him and you court the ruin of Yi Yin’s wards.

sentences.zh: 是以正名定本，使貴賤殊邈，然後國無陵肆之責，後嗣罔猜忌之嫌，群情絕異端之論，不逞杜覬覦之心；

translations.literal: Therefore correcting name and fixing root, making noble and base vastly separate, afterward the state has no blame for overbearing arrogance, later heirs lack suspicion and jealousy, crowd sentiment cuts off heterodox discussions, unruly ambition blocks covetous hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Name the true line, widen the gap between sovereign and subject, and the state escapes mutiny, the sons escape mutual murder, rumor dies, and ambition stays leashed;

sentences.zh: 於情雖違，於事雖儉，至於括囊遠圖，永保維城，可謂為之於其未有，治之於其未亂者也。

translations.literal: though in feeling it goes against, though in affairs it is stingy—as for tying the bag and far planning, forever protecting the shielding city wall, one may call it acting before not yet existing, ordering before not yet chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: painful as it looks in the ledger, it is the sealed purse and the long wall—the work done before crisis comes.

sentences.zh: 陳氏之評，其未達乎！〉

translations.literal: Chen Shou’s appraisal—has it not failed to reach that!〉
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou’s verdict never climbed to that height.〉
